Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. **I first ran for public office for two reasons. First, because I believe that every Virginian – and every American – should have the same shot at success that I had.**

I grew up in a middle class family, went to public school, and was the first in my family to graduate from college.

I then tried to get into business, and failed in about six weeks. My next attempt failed in six months. I was incredibly fortunate that my third venture broke through, and that I continued to see success throughout my career in the telecommunications industry.

Success should never depend on where you were born, who your parents are, or whether you had the right connections.

**Second, I got into politics because I believe you shouldn’t have to leave your hometown to find a world class job.** Success cannot depend on luck or geography. You should be able to build a good life in any zip code in Virginia.

It all comes down to this: Where you start should never determine where you end up. And it’s not lost on me – we’ve got a lot more work to do to make that a reality.

That’s why I’m asking Virginians to re-hire me one last time – and elect Democrats up and down the ballot who will stand up to this administration’s actions that are raising costs, fight for our communities, and offer a better path forward for our country.

body:
This proud mom thanks you for all you’ve done for my Gabby and for this movement.
#

Hello friend,
My name is Gloria Giffords. I’m Gabby Giffords’s mom. I stand in awe of my daughter.
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260827-1-b&t=1&akid=11767%2E3935704%2EE8qv0g)
I know every mom will tell you her child is perfect, but Gabby is just about as close as it comes. Growing up, she was always a good kid. She was a loyal friend. And to know Gabby Giffords is to know one thing: _Don’t ever — not for one moment — underestimate her._
Gabby’s one tough cookie. If she thought she could do something, she put her mind to it until it was done. And to anyone who thought she wasn’t capable of something..._well, she quickly proved them wrong._
Our nation has seen what Gabby is capable of since that awful morning in January 2011. It’s been a long road to recovery, but she continues fighting — not only for herself, but for families all across our country.
She inspires me every day, and I know I’m not alone.
**[Today, I am asking for you to join me in supporting Gabby’s work. GIFFORDS PAC is on the front lines to end the gun violence crisis in America, and they need more grassroots support ahead of the upcoming election. Anything you can spare will be put to work winning the most competitive of races.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260827-1-b&t=2&akid=11767%2E3935704%2EE8qv0g)

It shines a bright spotlight on what one man of courage can do -- and on what is at stake if we lose the Court. Let's be honest about the stakes. Control of the Senate hangs in the balance this November. The Senate is the body that confirms every single federal judge and every single Supreme Court justice. If the radical Left takes it back, the judicial nominations stop cold -- and the campaign to pack, punish and delegitimize the Court goes into overdrive. name: Cait Conley
subject: It's up to us
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY CAIT FOR NEW YORK
body:
| | | |
---
Peter, Look, when I first jumped into the race to beat Mike Lawler and flip NY-17, I really didn’t know what to expect. I knew that it was going to be a hard fight. We had an initial roadmap. But a lot of it was a shot in the dark. One thing I knew for sure: I would need a massive team behind me. More than a year and a half later, we’ve built that team. Last quarter more than 90% of our contributions came from grassroots gifts of less than $100. And with that support, we’ve built an operation that has turned this Lean-R district into a tossup. I’m incredibly proud of that, and I hope you are too. For 250 years our nation has gone through really dark times, really hard chapters. In these extraordinary moments, ordinary people rose up and chose to live with courage. They knew America and our democracy are worth fighting for. This chapter in American history is not yet written. Who we become, the values that define us, _that is up to us._ **We are the cavalry. We are who takes this country back.** It’s up to us to beat Lawler, flip NY-17, and take back the House for Democrats. I believe that we can do that. clean_body: | | | | Peter, Look, when I first jumped into the race to beat Mike Lawler and flip NY-17, I really didn’t know what to expect. I knew that it was going to be a hard fight. We had an initial roadmap. But a lot of it was a shot in the dark. One thing I knew for sure: I would need a massive team behind me. More than a year and a half later, we’ve built that team. Last quarter more than 90% of our contributions came from grassroots gifts of less than $100. And with that support, we’ve built an operation that has turned this Lean-R district into a tossup. I’m incredibly proud of that, and I hope you are too. For 250 years our nation has gone through really dark times, really hard chapters. In these extraordinary moments, ordinary people rose up and chose to live with courage. They knew America and our democracy are worth fighting for. This chapter in American history is not yet written. Who we become, the values that define us, that is up to us. We are the cavalry. We are who takes this country back. It’s up to us to beat Lawler, flip NY-17, and take back the House for Democrats. I believe that we can do that. But I know that this campaign can’t do it without you. So I’m humbly asking you to make a donation today. | If you've stored your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will process now. | | | | | | With gratitude and fire, Cait Conley | Follow us on social media! Polling Shows That The Race for Southwest Ohio is Near a Toss-Up

# For Immediate Release:
# August 26, 2026
---
| | |
# Contact:
# Press@EricConroy.com
---
| |
**NEW POLL SHOWS THAT THE RACE FOR OH-01 IN VIRTUAL TIE**
_Polling shows that the race for Southwest Ohio is near a toss-up_

---
| |

**Cincinnati, OH** — A new poll was conducted by Quantus Insights fielded August 21-24, 2026. The public poll shows that Greg Landsman leads Eric Conroy 47.9 to 44.6, a 3.3-point gap inside the survey’s own margin of error of 4.6 percent with the incumbent below 50 after 2 terms in Congress. The race for Ohio’s 1st Congressional District is in a virtual dead heat with undecided voters breaking to Conroy three to one. This shows that with 10 weeks to go, and the late movement belonging to Conroy, the race is anyone’s to win.
Conroy has the momentum behind him and the ability to flip this seat. Vice President JD Vance came to Cincinnati’s west side last week to campaign with Conroy. Additionally, National Republicans have already committed $5 million to help flip this seat. This investment comes at a time when, according to the survey, 38.3 percent of the district still has no opinion of the Republican nominee. The combined efforts of Conroy for Congress, and National Republicans will drive undecided voters to Conroy’s campaign.
_“The recent poll shows that our campaign is continuing to move in the right direction. Greg Landsman’s radical policies do not align with the values of this district. I will continue to champion common-sense policies that we know will make Cincinnati a better place for families to live and our region to thrive. I look forward to continuing to build on our momentum as we head into the fall”_ \- Eric Conroy
As we head into Labor Day, and the fall campaigning gets underway, it is clear that Eric Conroy has the momentum and national support needed to flip one of the most highly contested races in the country. The Conroy campaign will continue to work everyday to highlight Conroy’s message to voters: to create a more affordable and prosperous Southwest Ohio.
See more from Quantus Insights: [HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/7IS1XsVR1Cu?e=3f87e575ad&c2id=83ae238fa0f76420f201b2501cd8e566)
**Press Contact:** Collin Wojcik, Campaign Manager [Press@EricConroy.com](mailto:Press@EricConroy.com)

A heartfelt message from a veteran fighting for you.

A heartfelt message from a veteran fighting for you.
| [](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.)
---

Guided by my faith and surrounded by my wife, a high school sweetheart, and our beautiful children, I've experienced firsthand the blessings of America's greatest values.
[My life's mission has been to preserve this American greatness, first by serving in the Air Force and now as a constitutional lawyer fighting anyone who infringes upon our freedom.](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.-70kZ5m7GjvrPC2Op_Q)
Yet, I've seen time and time again how fragile our liberty is and the countless evil minds that seek to either take advantage of America or outright destroy it.
And let me tell you, the Radical Leftists have been especially relentless.
They would do anything for their woke agenda, but they would do absolutely nothing for our nation.
[As a proud seventh-generation Texan, I am beyond fed up.](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.-c6U9Qj2C3gyGg)
I'm fighting because Texas needs a leader who is unapologetically patriotic and is not afraid to say so. There are far too many politicians who are bought or compromised, having long forgotten why they decided to serve in the first place.
[President Trump has seen my commitment to America First, and I am honored to have his 100% endorsement. But the Radical Left is doubling down on its attacks against me because they know America First is their greatest enemy.](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.)
That's why I need your help, Peter.

# **Ted Cruz puts JD Vance on notice, signals potential 2028 challenge**
Sen. Ted Cruz told MS Now **[he'll "certainly be part of the discussion" for 2028,](https://substack.com/redirect/9ec75c54-089d-4b31-b05f-e3f6b1d53f37?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the clearest signal yet that he's considering another presidential run, as Republicans debate whether Vice President JD Vance has truly locked up the nomination despite polling well ahead of rivals like Marco Rubio and Cruz.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9ec75c54-089d-4b31-b05f-e3f6b1d53f37?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Cruz has carved out distinct positions from the administration,** including warning against Trump's tariffs, clashing with FCC Chair Brendan Carr over threats to revoke broadcast licenses, and pushing back against antisemitism within conservative circles -- differentiators strategists say could shape a campaign lane.
* **Trump has reportedly told donors privately he wants Vance to secure the nomination,** and Vance holds fundraising advantages as RNC finance chairman. Some Trump allies, including Alex Bruesewitz, dismissed Cruz's chances, while strategists remain split on whether he poses a real threat to Vance and Rubio.
* **Kalshi betting odds have Ted Cruz[at only 1.3%](https://substack.com/redirect/fb773017-b46a-4cb8-bd9d-a40bc8fee4bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to become the GOP's 2028 presidential nominee, with JD Vance currently at 43%.

# **Nigerian journalist imprisoned for exposing muslims murdering christians gives chilling warning**
Luka Binniyat, a Nigerian journalist jailed for over 80 days after **[reporting on muslim militants attacking Christians](https://substack.com/redirect/6df3a8cf-36bc-4f34-856e-d9a4f1ceb1f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in his home country, was cleared in May after a five-year legal battle, now he's free to report the truth.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6df3a8cf-36bc-4f34-856e-d9a4f1ceb1f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* "**You should not allow Islam to gain root in America.** They'll come there with values that are not your own, and even if they are a minority, they will eventually try to enforce their own religion, their own beliefs over the community," the 60-year-old Binniyat told The Daily Wire. "In Nigeria -- here in the Muslim-dominated areas -- Christians do not have rights."
* **Binniyat, who has documented mass killings and describes the violence in Nigeria 's religiously divided regions as genocide,** said Christians face systemic persecution from Islamist militant groups including Boko Haram and Fulani herdsmen, prompting the U.S. to designate Nigeria a country of particular concern in 2025.
* **His case drew support from groups including** Alliance Defending Freedom International and the Committee to Protect Journalists. Now free, Binniyat says he plans to keep reporting on Christian persecution and is urging Americans to resist what he views as the growing influence of Islam in the U.S.

body:
Attack ads, MAGA megadonors, and Donald Trump
#
Peter,
We’ll get right to it: Small Town PAC has just a few days left before our August fundraising deadline, and we still have ground to make up toward our $50,000 goal.
**The candidates we’re supporting aren’t running easy races.**
They’re competing in districts where Republicans are fighting hard to defend their power. They’re facing an onslaught of attack ads, MAGA megadonors, and opponents backed by Donald Trump’s political machine.
**That’s why we launched Small Town PAC:** to help Democratic candidates running to protect our communities win tough races.
We’re backing Jake Johnson in Minnesota, Sarah Trone Garriott in Iowa, and Rachel Wallace in Pennsylvania because they know how to listen, lead, and fight for the people they hope to represent.
Now, they need us to show up for them.

name: Jamie
subject: Question: Who Would Jesus Bomb?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jamie Davis for U
body:
I have read the Bible enough to know that Jesus preached a message of love, peace, and caring for the poor, the weak, and the sick. The answer is: nobody.
| | | | | [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001uwFz4v29WDS28l7hnuD1Xw7npsCoe3K1v8Q0pBemjqsIs-jEru3Exk37TuOoXb1-qDyFTn2_MrCB4nBCD6Fj6usFKKVCHkFnidATaSwgcgKPigQjG8sDuMN_0sjgOhw0n0Vdqc_1-PRF92torfNZcocepmOanYSTZKTtSInjyPAf30oT0fHFe5YBkDLTzd7agTxwLlUeUqTUWegsWV8x3ctwTCM2eFns&c=swu9b_R9f7zLyDG50fvW4y6v-7B83tNMBRce2K9En-xC-zUevtai8w==&ch=Eck3Q9S8KE0kstNXKigBtRVWlupEldGdN6R4GcpbhoEb14CQqHfSAg==)
---
| Peter,
It is a lesson America has learned too many times to repeat: politicians sending poor men and women to die in a war that helps no one but the arms dealer.
I am heartbroken by what I am seeing in the news. As a Christian, I know that my faith teaches me that all life is sacred. We are to pray for our enemies, not murder them and their children.
And what makes it worse is that the people pushing this war down Americans' throats are nine times out of ten claiming to be Christian. There were even reports of Generals telling troops this was a holy war waged as "part of God's plan":
---
| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001uwFz4v29WDS28l7hnuD1Xw7npsCoe3K1v8Q0pBemjqsIs-jEru3Exk37TuOoXb1-qDyFTn2_MrCB4nBCD6Fj6usFKKVCHkFnidATaSwgcgKPigQjG8sDuMN_0sjgOhw0n0Vdqc_1-PRF92torfNZcocepmOanYSTZKTtSInjyPAf30oT0fHFe5YBkDLTzd7agTxwLlUeUqTM0BERyBXyOvLVBnFHWHbj&c=swu9b_R9f7zLyDG50fvW4y6v-7B83tNMBRce2K9En-xC-zUevtai8w==&ch=Eck3Q9S8KE0kstNXKigBtRVWlupEldGdN6R4GcpbhoEb14CQqHfSAg==)
---
Now, I have read the Bible enough to know that Jesus preached a message of love, peace, and caring for the poor, the weak, and the sick.
So how can these politicians and pundits wear blinged-out diamond cross necklaces and AK-47 pins on their shirts, forsake diplomacy, resort to murder and violence, and then have the nerve to claim to be a Christian?
We are all shaped by our faith and worldview, and it seems obvious that the people pushing us into war worship money and power -- not Jesus.
I'm a Christian who respects everyone's right to exercise their own faith. That is what makes America such a beautiful place: religious freedom. But I see a lot of fake Christians right now in high places making some very evil choices.
When you are creating more cycles of endless war in the name of Jesus, we have a problem. Pete Hegseth, I'm talking to you.
Farmers don't start wars; they feed people. Farmers don't endorse billions in military spending while people go hungry.
[We need more farmers and fewer fake Christians in Washington to combat the greed-fueled policies hurting people here and abroad. Will you support my campaign for peace with a contribution of $10, $25, $50 or whatever you can do?](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001uwFz4v29WDS28l7hnuD1Xw7npsCoe3K1v8Q0pBemjqsIs-jEru3Exk37TuOoXb1-qBtkXYtSto-Gw5AdmPe_ZeJFhu78l8w-c6ls3vIoy8qa17uAASx_5yG_jIBx0upfjVVIPj3CdeojWbz672RpODvt7_1u04fJXdDdL24xKl--k9G-GoKw4yT4OUKRqfUgaHT87Xz7_jQ4Tu3kjB4NdQprI0jUO0bk5siphgkagRY=&c=swu9b_R9f7zLyDG50fvW4y6v-7B83tNMBRce2K9En-xC-zUevtai8w==&ch=Eck3Q9S8KE0kstNXKigBtRVWlupEldGdN6R4GcpbhoEb14CQqHfSAg==)

That’s me... pushing shopping carts at my first job.

I was a working-class kid long before I was ever a member of Congress. **And that first job taught me something I’ll never forget:**

The people who keep this country running usually don’t get a seat at the tables of power.

That’s why I became an organizer. That’s why I ran for Congress. And that’s why I keep fighting for young, working-class, and marginalized people to finally get a real say in our future.

The truth is billionaires, corporations, and their hired hands in power don’t like it when someone like me makes it to Congress. _Because they know what it means when working people start to organize, speak up, and win._

**It gets a _hell of a lot harder_ to ignore us.**

And that’s exactly why **your** support matters. Grassroots donations help power this people-first movement, build our organizing strength, and keep us fighting for a Congress that looks like the rest of us.

| | Dear Friend, You are invited to a Red Carpet evening unlike any other. On September 17, join us at the iconic Southfork Ranch in Dallas, Texas—the legendary home made famous by Dallas—for a One Night Only live production of Our American Story. Written and produced by Kimberly Fletcher, Founder and President of Moms for America, and Academy Award-winning actor Jon Voight, Our American Story takes audiences on an unforgettable theatrical journey through 250 years of American history. Through dramatic storytelling, cinematic visuals, live performances, powerful music, and extraordinary American voices, the story of our nation comes alive on stage. The production features prerecorded performances by:Kelsey Grammer • Jon Voight • Gary Sinise • Kirk Cameron

| | But this is more than a night at the theater. It is a celebration of who we are as Americans—and a reminder of the story we have a responsibility to pass on. For generations, Americans have shared a common understanding of the principles that shaped our nation: faith, liberty, courage, personal responsibility, and the belief that freedom is worth preserving. Yet too many young Americans are growing up without knowing the remarkable story of how thirteen struggling colonies became a nation founded on the extraordinary promise of liberty. Our American Story brings that history to life. Instead of experiencing history as a textbook, audiences are invited to experience it as a living story—the people who built this nation, the principles that guided them, the sacrifices they made, and the providence that carried America forward. And there is no better setting for this special evening than Southfork Ranch.

clean_body: September 17, Southfork Ranch in Dallas, Texas | | Can 't see this message? | | | | | | One Night.One Stage.One Unforgettable American Story. | | | Dear Friend, You are invited to a Red Carpet evening unlike any other. On September 17, join us at the iconic Southfork Ranch in Dallas, Texas—the legendary home made famous by Dallas—for a One Night Only live production of Our American Story. Written and produced by Kimberly Fletcher, Founder and President of Moms for America, and Academy Award-winning actor Jon Voight, Our American Story takes audiences on an unforgettable theatrical journey through 250 years of American history. Through dramatic storytelling, cinematic visuals, live performances, powerful music, and extraordinary American voices, the story of our nation comes alive on stage. The production features prerecorded performances by:Kelsey Grammer • Jon Voight • Gary Sinise • Kirk Cameron | | | | | | But this is more than a night at the theater. It is a celebration of who we are as Americans—and a reminder of the story we have a responsibility to pass on. For generations, Americans have shared a common understanding of the principles that shaped our nation: faith, liberty, courage, personal responsibility, and the belief that freedom is worth preserving. Yet too many young Americans are growing up without knowing the remarkable story of how thirteen struggling colonies became a nation founded on the extraordinary promise of liberty. Our American Story brings that history to life. Instead of experiencing history as a textbook, audiences are invited to experience it as a living story—the people who built this nation, the principles that guided them, the sacrifices they made, and the providence that carried America forward. And there is no better setting for this special evening than Southfork Ranch. | | | | | Walk the Red Carpet. Gather with fellow Americans who believe our story is worth preserving. Experience a production designed to inspire a new generation to understand, appreciate, and carry forward the American legacy. This is a One Night Only experience. And we want you there. September 17, 2026 | Southfork Ranch | Dallas, Texas Reserve your tickets today and be part of America's story. | | | | Visit our social accounts | | | | This email was sent from .

We’ve shared movie sets and red carpets — but we’ve also shared picket lines, and even handcuffs on the steps of the Capitol for refusing to stay silent about the climate crisis. **I am proud to call her a dear friend. And I am even more proud of the work she and her team are doing right now at JanePAC. They remind me that change is still possible, and I’m reaching out today because they need our help.** What Donald Trump and his buddies are doing to this country isn't subtle anymore. They are consolidating power with ruthless efficiency, stacking every branch of government with allies, and rewarding the fossil fuel billionaires and corporate donors who scratch their backs while ordinary families are left to breathe the pollution and foot the bill. And yet, when I start to feel the weight of all of that, I think about Jane and this movement she has built. Since founding Jane Fonda Climate PAC, Jane and her team have helped elect over 250 climate champions from school boards to Congress who fight for our communities and can't be bought or bullied into silence. These last few months alone, JanePAC’s endorsed candidates won hard-fought primaries from California to Michigan to Pennsylvania and beyond. These weren’t easy races. But they were able to invest in and support courageous leaders because grassroots supporters like you showed up. **So that's why I'm coming to you today. in person.

election. Our volunteer stayed with her on the phone as she found her

next day.

vote because of his record. Our volunteer explained he absolutely
could — and the man broke down in tears. He’s now spreading the word

Sudan's army shoots down drone that crossed into Sudan from Ethiopia. Sudan's RSF closes markets and cuts off internet in West Kordofan amid intensifying fighting. U.S. official condemns Sudanese Army strike in Chad. Democratic Republic of the Congo Suspends 11 Universities in M23-Held Goma and Bukavu. # Palestine
* **Israeli drone strikes wound Palestinians in Gaza City and Khan Younis:**
* Israeli drones [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/4160a126-6333-40f1-b7dd-c251d43a0bda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a home in western Gaza City on Thursday morning, injuring several people, WAFA reported.
* A separate drone strike also hit a tent sheltering displaced people in Khan Younis, in the southern part of the Strip, wounding several..
* **Israeli settlers expand outpost in occupied West Bank; five Palestinians wounded in Hebron and Jerusalem:**
* **Bethlehem:** Israeli settlers, under the protection of Israeli forces, [continued expanding](https://substack.com/redirect/ddb11bea-275d-491f-b269-8e5ee3df25fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an outpost in the Ush Ghrab area on Thursday, bringing in mobile homes and installing them at the site, WAFA reported. Settlers also raised Israeli flags along the road. The area, which includes an Israeli military base, had been designated around 15 years ago for a children's hospital serving the Bethlehem governorate, but the project was never completed after settlers established an outpost there.
* **East Jerusalem:** Israeli soldiers [tear gassed](https://substack.com/redirect/46009704-8e28-40bd-ac4a-719cc0be1de8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and fired upon Palestinians in Beit Anan on Wednesday evening, northwest of East Jerusalem, and injured two Palestinians during the raid, one of whom was shot in the knee.
* Israeli authorities [tightened](https://substack.com/redirect/dbb55d21-ed12-4299-9c66-d5b213c96560?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) movement restrictions on Palestinian communities northwest of occupied East Jerusalem, requiring residents of Nabi Samwil, Beit Iksa and the Khalayleh neighborhood to obtain special permits to enter and leave their communities, with some families removed from lists allowing them access to their homes, according to the Jerusalem Governorate.
* **Hebron:** Israeli soldiers [shot](https://substack.com/redirect/3894035d-86c7-44b1-a61c-d7adbf03a7f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and wounded two women and a 14-year-old girl in Al-Kamel on Wednesday night, WAFA reported, during a raid on the town.**** The women were returning from a wedding when soldiers fired heavily at their vehicle without warning, according to the town's mayor and husband of one of the wounded women. He said his 58-year-old wife and the 14-year-old girl suffered serious injuries to the face, while a 30-year-old woman was wounded by shrapnel.
* Also in the Hebron governorate,**** Israeli settlers [chased](https://substack.com/redirect/75d88432-5d1e-4ee8-915d-efbc3588ccde?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Palestinian shepherds off their land near the village of Masafer Yatta on Wednesday, with several other incidents of theft, harassment, and military assistance of settlers reported in the area.
* **UN: Israel has killed at least 100 Palestinians in Gaza in last two weeks:** Israeli air strikes since August 12 have [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/59e7deb9-9498-48c1-a6ab-0ddd7fae0af8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at least 100 Palestinians and wounded 400 others in Gaza, Ramiz Alakbarov, the acting UN special coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, told the UN Security Council on Tuesday, noting that conditions remained "dire despite a nearly year-old ceasefire."
* **Haaretz: Israel cultivating network of armed militias across Gaza:** A Haaretz investigation based on Israeli soldiers' testimony, Palestinian sources, UN information, and satellite imagery [revealed](https://substack.com/redirect/04f598ef-7bbc-445f-9b3b-8c0432156ab1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the extent of Israel's cooperation with armed Palestinian militias in Gaza. Haaretz identified five prominent groups operating in areas under Israeli control, with apparent activity at a sixth location.
* The militias, which have regularly clashed with Hamas fighters, operate from compounds near Israeli military outposts and are integrated into IDF operations, with call signs on army radio networks and positions marked on military maps. Soldiers said Israel has built compounds for some groups, with others saying the IDF has provided artillery and drone support.
* Haaretz also documented accounts of militia members looting and burning Palestinian homes and helping force residents from their communities. "You see the State of Israel, the IDF and Shin Bet sending armed, trained militias to commit war crimes, and I'm the one who has to protect them during their operations so they don't get hurt," an Israeli air force officer said.
* **Israeli court acquits settler who attacked French nun:** The**** Jerusalem Magistrate Court [acquitted](https://substack.com/redirect/142b3822-fecd-4b0a-8d56-96c55096960a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday Yona Schreiber, a settler from the occupied West Bank settlement of Peduel, who assaulted a French Catholic nun near Jerusalem's Old City earlier this year, finding him not responsible because of "mental illness."
* Schreiber attacked the 48-year-old nun and researcher in April, pushing her to the ground, kicking her in the head and wounding her outside the Cenacle on Mount Zion.
* **Mladenov discusses Trump 's Board Gaza plan before UNSC: **Nickolay Mladenov, the "High Representative" for the Gaza Board of Peace, [spoke](https://substack.com/redirect/1f6d3eb3-dafc-4c75-ac9d-416e8ff0e51a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) before the the UN Security Council on Wednesday, telling the body that Hamas's decision to disarm and transfer authority to a transitional administration would be an "opportunity to dramatically improve life in a sustainable way for Palestinians in Gaza".
* In his testimony, he hailed Hamas' acceptance of "complete demilitarization" of the Strip. Hamas has stressed that it has agreed for heavy weapons to be restricted and stored under the authority of a Palestinian committee governing Gaza.
* Mladenov claimed that "Three things must be in place for the process to move forward: the International Stabilization Force must deploy; Israel's undertakings under the Sharm el-Sheikh protocol must be implemented; and Hamas must adhere to its commitments."
* The representative said, in light of recent attacks on the Strip, that "Gaza does not have it in it to bear another catastrophe." He tiptoed around Israel's responsibility for carrying out these attacks, noting that Israel was "not a signatory" to the Board's plans, having only affirmed its commitments verbally, and claimed that Israel's present use of force in the Strip did not pose an "immediate threat" to peace.

This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Palestine Israeli drone strikes wound Palestinians in Gaza City and Khan Younis: Israeli drones a home in western Gaza City on Thursday morning, injuring several people, WAFA reported. A separate drone strike also hit a tent sheltering displaced people in Khan Younis, in the southern part of the Strip, wounding several.. Israeli settlers expand outpost in occupied West Bank; five Palestinians wounded in Hebron and Jerusalem: Bethlehem: Israeli settlers, under the protection of Israeli forces, an outpost in the Ush Ghrab area on Thursday, bringing in mobile homes and installing them at the site, WAFA reported. Settlers also raised Israeli flags along the road. The area, which includes an Israeli military base, had been designated around 15 years ago for a children's hospital serving the Bethlehem governorate, but the project was never completed after settlers established an outpost there. East Jerusalem: Israeli soldiers and fired upon Palestinians in Beit Anan on Wednesday evening, northwest of East Jerusalem, and injured two Palestinians during the raid, one of whom was shot in the knee. Israeli authorities movement restrictions on Palestinian communities northwest of occupied East Jerusalem, requiring residents of Nabi Samwil, Beit Iksa and the Khalayleh neighborhood to obtain special permits to enter and leave their communities, with some families removed from lists allowing them access to their homes, according to the Jerusalem Governorate. Hebron: Israeli soldiers and wounded two women and a 14-year-old girl in Al-Kamel on Wednesday night, WAFA reported, during a raid on the town. The women were returning from a wedding when soldiers fired heavily at their vehicle without warning, according to the town's mayor and husband of one of the wounded women. He said his 58-year-old wife and the 14-year-old girl suffered serious injuries to the face, while a 30-year-old woman was wounded by shrapnel. Also in the Hebron governorate,** Israeli settlers Palestinian shepherds off their land near the village of Masafer Yatta on Wednesday, with several other incidents of theft, harassment, and military assistance of settlers reported in the area. UN: Israel has killed at least 100 Palestinians in Gaza in last two weeks: Israeli air strikes since August 12 have at least 100 Palestinians and wounded 400 others in Gaza, Ramiz Alakbarov, the acting UN special coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, told the UN Security Council on Tuesday, noting that conditions remained "dire despite a nearly year-old ceasefire." Haaretz: Israel cultivating network of armed militias across Gaza: A Haaretz investigation based on Israeli soldiers' testimony, Palestinian sources, UN information, and satellite imagery the extent of Israel's cooperation with armed Palestinian militias in Gaza. Haaretz identified five prominent groups operating in areas under Israeli control, with apparent activity at a sixth location. The militias, which have regularly clashed with Hamas fighters, operate from compounds near Israeli military outposts and are integrated into IDF operations, with call signs on army radio networks and positions marked on military maps. Soldiers said Israel has built compounds for some groups, with others saying the IDF has provided artillery and drone support. Haaretz also documented accounts of militia members looting and burning Palestinian homes and helping force residents from their communities. "You see the State of Israel, the IDF and Shin Bet sending armed, trained militias to commit war crimes, and I'm the one who has to protect them during their operations so they don't get hurt," an Israeli air force officer said. Israeli court acquits settler who attacked French nun: The** Jerusalem Magistrate Court Wednesday Yona Schreiber, a settler from the occupied West Bank settlement of Peduel, who assaulted a French Catholic nun near Jerusalem's Old City earlier this year, finding him not responsible because of "mental illness." Schreiber attacked the 48-year-old nun and researcher in April, pushing her to the ground, kicking her in the head and wounding her outside the Cenacle on Mount Zion. Mladenov discusses Trump 's Board Gaza plan before UNSC: Nickolay Mladenov, the "High Representative" for the Gaza Board of Peace, before the the UN Security Council on Wednesday, telling the body that Hamas's decision to disarm and transfer authority to a transitional administration would be an "opportunity to dramatically improve life in a sustainable way for Palestinians in Gaza". In his testimony, he hailed Hamas' acceptance of "complete demilitarization" of the Strip. Hamas has stressed that it has agreed for heavy weapons to be restricted and stored under the authority of a Palestinian committee governing Gaza. Mladenov claimed that "Three things must be in place for the process to move forward: the International Stabilization Force must deploy; Israel's undertakings under the Sharm el-Sheikh protocol must be implemented; and Hamas must adhere to its commitments." The representative said, in light of recent attacks on the Strip, that "Gaza does not have it in it to bear another catastrophe." He tiptoed around Israel's responsibility for carrying out these attacks, noting that Israel was "not a signatory" to the Board's plans, having only affirmed its commitments verbally, and claimed that Israel's present use of force in the Strip did not pose an "immediate threat" to peace. Mladenov Israel's policy on shelter, in light of the approaching winter, "not acceptable," and urged Israel to "allow better shelter into the Strip for dignity, for health, and for safety." Mladenov also issued a rare criticism of Israel's continued airstrikes on Gaza, though he refrained from framing them as targeting civilians: "After three years of war and 20 years of military operations, I ask, will another strike on a munitions depot stop Hamas from rearming or tightening its grip on Gaza?" he said. "It will not. It only delays the demilitarization that would happen, and it obstructs the civilian transition that should take place to ensure that remilitarization will not be possible in the future." Israel's deputy UN ambassador, Noa Furman, also before the body, saying that Hamas's "disarmament must come first" before Gaza's reconstruction can begin, while still claiming Israel remains committed to Trump's plan. Gaza Board of Peace "failing," development chief tells Security Council: Athena Rayburn, the executive director of the Association of International Development Agencies, the U.S.-led Gaza Board of Peace for failing to stop Israel's daily attacks on the Strip before the Security Council on Wednesday. She said that the Board had, as an institution, failed to provide "immediate protection, relief and safety for the civilian population" in Gaza in the short term, and seemed unable to move Gaza towards "the end of Israel's unlawful presence and the realization of the Palestinian people's inalienable right to self-determination." Rayburn noted that, "the rights of Palestinians in Gaza have been made subordinate to the far-reaching, capricious and arbitrary requirements of its occupier," and called the arrangement "untenable." Palestinian envoy tells UNSC that Israeli annexation has reached point of no return: Riyad Mansour, the permanent observer of Palestine to the United Nations, also before the UN Security Council on Wednesday, telling the body that Israel's annexation of Palestinian land has reached a point of no return. "Annexation has long been under way, but Israel has now crossed the Rubicon when it comes to full-fledged, full-blown annexation with the release of the tenders for the E1 plan," Mansour said. The E1 settlement project would effectively divide the occupied West Bank in two. Canada revokes Jerusalem deputy mayor 's visa: Canada has travel authorization for Jerusalem's Deputy Mayor Arieh King over his activities on behalf of illegal settlements on Tuesday, leading King to cancel a planned visit to Toronto and Montreal. King, an especially vocal advocate of settlement in occupied East Jerusalem, had been scheduled to attend a fundraising event in Canada for his settlement initiatives, the report said. Iran Tanker hit by projectile while transiting Hormuz: A tanker was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz Tuesday, setting the vessel on fire, the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency on Thursday. The attack caused no injuries to the crew and the fire has since been put out, local authorities said. Iranian warship confronts vessel in Hormuz: A "large Iranian Warship" an Indian ship attempting to transit the southern U.S.-backed route in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, Iran's Fars news agency reported. The ship was deterred from passing through the Strait after receiving a warning, the agency said, alleging that no traffic had been observed through the southern route in the 24 hours preceding the confrontation. Drones shot down over Iraqi Kurdistan: At least one drone was the village of Badalyan in Iraq's Erbil governorate on Wednesday, according to Al Jazeera, which reported an attack on the area by two drones. The downed drone sparked a fire in the region. No casualties were reported from the attack. The attack reportedly targeted facilities belonging to Iranian Kurdish opposition parties. Qatari, Iranian FMs meet in Tehran, discuss mine clearing and potential Hormuz corridor: Qatar's Foreign Minister, Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Tehran on Thursday, a meeting during which, "the latest developments in the regional situation were reviewed, along with the efforts being made to reduce escalation and create appropriate conditions for dialogue," according to a statement from Qatar's Foreign Ministry. During the meeting, the ministers also discussed a "joint project" to clear mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and a "proposed interim framework" that would include the creation of a temporary shipping corridor through the Strait, according to the statement. U.S. officials signal readiness to attack Iran, though "prefer diplomacy": U.S. President Donald Trump Al Jazeera Wednesday he was "not in a hurry" to continue talks with Iran, and that he had "no time schedule" for their resumption. In a phone interview with the outlet, he claimed that military and economic measures against Iran had "both" been effective. During an interview on Newsmax, War Secretary Pete Hegseth assumed a more belligerent tone, saying that "by no means" had the U.S. "foreclosed using kinetic strikes anywhere in the Strait of Hormuz." At a press conference with International Atomic Energy Agency Chief Rafael Grossi, Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the administration "prefers diplomacy" with Iran, though it would strike Iran again to destroy its nuclear facilities "if necessary." Iran says "hostile" Persian-language media could be "potential military targets": Brigadier-General Abolfazl Shekarchi, the spokesperson for Iran's armed forces, several Persian-language media outlets, including BBC Persian, Iran International, and Radio Farda, of direct connections to "Mossad, the CIA and enemy intelligence organizations," on Wednesday, and said that these outlets and their employees could be considered military targets, according to AFP citing remarks on state television.. IAEA 's chief says no "solid evidence" that Iran is rebuilding nuclear facilities: International Atomic Energy Agency head Rafael Grossi the Argentinian paper Clarin on Wednesday that there is no "solid evidence" to suggest that Iran is rebuilding its nuclear facilities following U.S. and Israeli attacks. "The facilities have suffered significant damage" he noted, saying that, though there is a possibility that Iran had begun to rebuild "some of their infrastructure," no evidence exists of a resumed nuclear activity. Grossi also told the paper that Iran's existing stockpile of highly enriched uranium remains buried following U.S. strikes during the Twelve-Day War last year. Iran's atomic energy chief Mohammad Eslami told Iran's IRNA News Agency on Wednesday that the IAEA would not be able to inspect Iranian nuclear sites that have suffered attacks in recent months until it develops a specific inspection protocol for the sites which ensures their security. Araghchi calls U.S. sanctions "state and economic terrorism": Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi the newest wave of U.S. sanctions an "act of state and economic terrorism" in a Wednesday letter to the UN secretary-general, the Security Council and all UN member states. Araghchi accused the U.S. of seeking to "cut Iran's lawful economic ties with other states" after failing to achieve its objectives through war or persuade other countries to join its campaign. "The sanctions deliberately harm civilians by restricting access to food, medicine, medical equipment, energy and other essentials, violating rights including the rights to life, health, food and an adequate standard of living," he wrote in the letter. Iran cannot import enough petrol as a result of U.S. blockade: Iran has been to import enough petrol to offset reduced domestic production as a result of the U.S. naval blockade, Mohammad Jafar Ghaempah, a senior official, told IRNA. Pakistan says it is not bound by U.S. sanctions on Iran, and rejects reports that army chief visited Tehran as Trump 's envoy: At a press conference in Islamabad on Thursday, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Taher Andarab Pakistan does not believe Washington's unilateral sanctions on Tehran adhere to international law and that issues should be resolved through dialogue. At the same conference, Andarab rejected reports that its army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, travelled to Iran earlier this week on Trump's behalf, calling the claims "misleading and factually incorrect." He said Munir's visit was undertaken "purely in the context and backdrop of Pakistan's ongoing role as mediator." Yemen Ansarallah strikes Mokha port and Yemen 's western coast: Yemen's Ansarallah fired ballistic missiles at Mokha port on Wednesday, with at least three missiles striking the port area and a fourth landing toward the Al-Barah intersection, a source from the Saudi-backed Yemeni army told Al Jazeera. At least five additional missiles struck the Al-Khawkhah area of Hodeidah governorate on Yemen's western coast. There were no immediate reports of casualties or the extent of damage. Saudi-backed forces claim seizure of vessel carrying drone equipment to Ansarallah: Yemeni naval forces they seized a vessel carrying drone-making equipment off the coast of Mokha in the Red Sea on Wednesday evening, alleging the shipment had been smuggled by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and was bound for Ansarallah, according to the Aden-based Saba news agency, Naval patrols also opened fire on five Ansarallah boats approaching islands overlooking the international shipping lane, forcing them north toward Hodeidah, and shot down a reconnaissance drone. Lebanon Newlywed woman killed as Israel strikes southern Lebanon: A newlywed woman was killed and others wounded Thursday when Israeli warplanes and destroyed her home in the center of Arabsalim in the Nabatieh district, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. The woman had been married just 48 hours ago. Israeli warplanes struck the town again less than 10 minutes later, while an Israeli drone carried out two strikes on Nabatieh Al-Fawqa. Earlier Thursday, Israeli warplanes two strikes on the Ali Al-Taher hills on the eastern outskirts of Nabatieh al-Fawqa, firing several missiles that caused large explosions. In Marjayoun, Israeli forces accompanied by tanks and military bulldozers into the western outskirts of Mays Al-Jabal, in the Al-Dabsh area, as artillery struck several homes. Israeli forces also set homes on fire and bulldozed agricultural tents. U.S. News U.S. designates three left-wing groups in Europe "terrorists", including UK's Palestine Action: The U.S. State Department three European left-wing groups as "transnational terrorist organizations." Two of the groups, Palestine Action and Masar Badil , are focused on activism in support of Palestine, and the third, Autistici Inventati , offers free digital tools to leftists around the world. The U.S. Treasury Department announced, in coordination with the State Department, that it would be imposing sanctions on the groups, allowing its OFAC to block the U.S. property of anyone who supports or is linked to any of the groups. Palestine Action, which describes itself as a "direct action movement committed to ending global complicity with Israel's genocidal apartheid regime", has also been banned in the UK, where it is based. The UK ban has been criticized by numerous human rights groups, including Amnesty International. In a statement to Al Jazeera, Palestine Action cofounder Huda Ammori has lambasted the U.S. for blacklisting the group as a "Specially Designated Global Terrorist", saying it should serve as "a wake-up call to anyone who cares about free speech and civil liberties". ICE agent Christian Castro released from Texas jail: Federal JudgeFernando Rodriguez Jr. ruled Wednesday in favor of Texas Gov. Greg Abbott in an extradition dispute with Minnesota, finding Minnesota had not proven Abbott acted wrongfully by delaying action on a request to return ICE agent Christian Castro to face four charges of assault in Minnesota. Rodriguez's decision in Castro's release from a Texas jail Thursday under the state's 90-day detention limit. Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty warned the ruling risks letting Castro flee to Mexico, where he has discussed marrying a woman and buying a house. Minnesota Attorney GeneralKeith Ellison, a Democrat, said he disagreed with Rodriguez's ruling and would "continue litigating this case." Maine GOP governor nominee says he 'll seek ICE presence at polling places: Bobby Charles, the Republican nominee for Maine governor, supporters at an August 20 event that he plans to ask White House border czar Tom Homan to send ICE agents and U.S. marshals to Maine polling places ahead of this fall's election, according to audio first reported by the Bangor Daily News and cited by NBC News. Charles later said the goal was to "prevent violence," "intimidation," and "illegality" at voting locations. Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows said in response to Charles's remarks that ICE agents are legally barred from polling places. Van Hollen forces Senate resolution demanding accounting of Israel 's West Bank human rights record: Sen. Chris Van Hollen to introduce a privileged resolution Thursday, co-signed by 10 Senate Democrats, that would require the Trump administration to provide Congress with a detailed accounting of Israel's human rights practices in the West Bank within 30 days, forcing a Senate vote regardless of Republican leadership's cooperation. The resolution focuses on at least nine American citizens killed in the West Bank since January 2022, includingAysenur Ezgi Eygi and journalist Shireen Abu Akleh. Van Hollen said "if the United States Senate shines a spotlight on this, we will save lives." Pentagon panel claims it found "hidden" documents on Afghanistan withdrawal: Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell , who also chairs War SecretaryPete Hegseth 's review panel investigating the 2021 Afghanistan withdrawal, Wednesday the probe uncovered "highly relevant, classified documents" that had been "stashed and hidden away in safes where they would not be found." Parnell did not disclose the documents' contents or say when they might be made public, adding only that "after the team reviewed these documents, it became clear why someone tried to hide them." Parnell's panel, launched by Hegseth in May 2025, has reviewed 9 million documents and completed interviews with military figures involved in the withdrawal, which Parnell has argued will be more thorough than a 2024 congressional Republican report he criticized as "over-classified." West Point professor sues, says he was fired for refusing to omit climate science : Dr. Adam Kalkstein , a tenured West Point science professor, is the U.S. Military Academy after he says he was ordered to cut information about human-caused climate change from his curriculum and was later told his contract would not be renewed, according to The New York Times. Kalkstein, described by his attorney as a conservative Republican who believes understanding climate change is essential for national security matters like Arctic competition with Russia, said Brig. Gen. Shane R. Reeves , then West Point's dean, stormed out of a meeting after Kalkstein declined a suggestion he resign. The lawsuit accuses the academy of violating his First Amendment rights by requiring him "to omit a massive, fundamental, essential component of the course and to defy science." Navy sailor who jumped overboard USS Abraham Lincoln faces disciplinary charges: A sailor who threw himself overboard from the USS Abraham Lincoln earlier this month in what his wife described as a suicide attempt is now facing disciplinary charges from the Navy, to MS NOW. The sailor is accused of "absence without leave" and "malingering," which is defined as a service member "intentionally faking an illness or hurting themselves to avoid work, duty or service," according to the sailor's wife and charging documents. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Russia threatens to strike UK military targets: Russia Thursday that it could strike British military installations and equipment "in Ukraine and beyond its borders" in response to Ukrainian attacks inside Russia using British-supplied Storm Shadow cruise missiles. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova accused London of being "one step away" from legal complicity in what Moscow calls terrorism against Russian civilians and warned that Britain's policy could escalate the war "to an entirely new level." The threat followed Russia's accusation that Ukraine fired Storm Shadows at a shopping center in Russian-controlled Donetsk, wounding civilians, including children. It also came days after Britain announced that Kyiv would receive classified technology to begin producing the long-range missiles domestically. Israeli forces fire shells near Syrian town: Israeli forces three artillery shells near the Syrian town of Beit Jinn, southwest of Damascus on Wednesday, the Syrian news agency ANHA reported. Israeli forces reportedly fired the shells from the occupied Golan Heights towards a strategic hill overlooking the town. Israeli forces have previously used the hill to stage raids on Beit Jinn, which an Israeli drone struck on Saturday. Sudan 's army shoots down drone that crossed into Sudan from Ethiopia: Sudan's army Thursday it shot down a hostile drone that crossed into southeastern Blue Nile state from Ethiopian territory, intercepting it north of Sarkam, marking the third such incident reported in the border area in recent days, according to Sudan Tribune. The military did not identify the drone's operator, origin, or intended target. RSF closes markets and cuts off internet in West Kordofan amid intensifying fighting: Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) indefinitely all public markets and cut off Starlink internet access in Al-Nuhud, West Kordofan on Wednesday, according to the Dar Hamar Emergency Response Room, a local volunteer group. The group warned that the blackout disables mobile banking and remittance services residents depend on amid severe cash shortages. It also accused RSF forces of widespread looting and harassment and urged international humanitarian organizations to intervene U.S. official condemns Sudanese Army strike in Chad: U.S. advisor Massad Boulos Sudan's military for airstrikes inside Chad, writing on X on Wednesday that there is "absolutely no justification for expanding the violence beyond Sudan's borders." The Sudanese army says the August 20 strikes hit a Rapid Support Forces resupply convoy of roughly 200 combat vehicles moving from Libya's Kufra region, Sudan Tribune reported. Chad's army confirmed that aircraft "belonging to the Sudanese Armed Forces or forces supporting them" bombed a convoy more than 100 km inside its territory, and condemned it as a violation of its sovereignty. DR Congo Suspends 11 Universities in M23-Held Goma and Bukavu: The Democratic Republic of Congo has academic operations until further notice at 11 public universities and institutes in Goma and Bukavu, two eastern cities controlled by the Rwanda-backed M23, the AFP reported on Wednesday. Registration, teaching, examinations and deliberations are suspended for 2026-2027, with students in their final year of school being sent to Kinshasa to complete their studies. Taiwanese parliament rejects government 's $6.6 billion military drone plan: Taiwan's opposition-controlled parliament the government's proposed $6.6 billion special budget to acquire roughly 210,000 military drones through 2031, instead approving a smaller plan to acquire drones over the next six years. The government has argued the expansion is urgent given lessons from the wars in Ukraine and Iran and the growing threat from China. The defense ministry said its original plan had been coordinated with unnamed allied countries, while the United States has strongly backed Taiwan's effort to build a large domestic drone force. Death toll from Nepal-China border floods rises to at least 353, with 826 missing : Nepal Police at least 353 dead and 826 missing Thursday following a catastrophic glacial-collapse flood that swept through communities the day before, according to CBS News, while Chinese state broadcaster CCTV separately reported 558 people missing in Tibet, including 260 foreigners. The tourism board later said 27 foreign nationals, including two Americans, had been rescued from Nepal's Rasuwa district. The U.S. Geological Survey revised its initial assessment of a magnitude 4.4 earthquake to instead identify a magnitude 5.2 glacial collapse as the cause. Nigerian kidnappers collected nearly $5.8 million in ransom over past year, report finds : Nigerian kidnappers roughly $5.79 million in ransom payments between July 2025 and June 2026, according to a report from security consultancy SBM Intelligence. 7,825 people were kidnapped between July 2025 and June 2026, up 66% from the year before, according to the report, with at least 1,142 people killed in the region. A faction of Boko Haram collected 90% of recorded ransom payments, roughly 7 billion naira, largely from two mass kidnappings involving more than 300 victims each. Forest fires kill 12 in northeastern Algeria, dozens injured : Forest fires 12 people and injured dozens across northeastern Algeria's Bejaia, Jijel, and Tizi Ouzou provinces Wednesday, according to Interior Minister Said Sayoud. 54 people were being treated for burns, including six serious cases, at a hospital in Bejaia, where an eight-year-old boy and a 22-year-old woman were among the dead, according to local radio. Algeria has recorded nearly 2,000 fires nationwide this year, part of a pattern authorities and scientists say climate change is intensifying through more frequent droughts and heat. WHO: Uganda 's Ebola outbreak over, but DRC's continues to rise: The World Health Organization declared Uganda's Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak over, following the country's own July 28 declaration after 20 cases and two deaths, but WHO official Dr. Marie Roseline Belizaire the outbreak remains uncontrolled in neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo, where cases continue to climb despite some progress. Hey folks,
This one is wild. The Tate brothers built an entire online identity around wealth, power, masculinity, and being untouchable--and now, according to the reporting discussed here, their own legal defense is arguing that parts of that image were basically theater. We get into what that says about their movement, their legal strategy, and the young men who were sold the fantasy.

* [**00:07:21**] Why the broader MAGA influencer ecosystem largely isn't riding to the Tate brothers' rescue--and what that tells us about grievance, money, and self-interest.
* [**00:10:13**] We break down the Russia angle, the arguments coming from the Tates' legal team, and why I think their public defense keeps falling apart.
* [**00:13:15**] A message directly to young men: confidence is good. Risk is good. But fear and doubt are human--and pretending you never feel them isn't strength. It's delusion.

This episode is bigger than two internet personalities. It's about the fantasy they sold, the people who bought into it, and what happens when an online persona collides with the real world. A $1.2 trillion missile shield over America, to be built over twenty years. They call it the Golden Dome.

Trillions in military hardware orders are now stacking up faster than they can be filled. And nearly every aircraft in that pipeline, along with almost every plane already in the sky, depends on parts from one Cleveland company most people have never heard of.

This isn't speculation. The Pentagon's own auditors examined 47 of its parts and found that on 39 of them, no other producer exists anywhere on Earth. Its CEO says 90% of sales come from unique proprietary products. A congressional investigation found margins on some parts past 4,000%.

That law locked Virginia into a fixed timeline to shut down power plants, with **no real plan for the data center boom that followed.**
Six years later, Virginia doesn't produce enough of its own power. We're importing electricity from coal plants in West Virginia, and hundreds of miles of new transmission lines are cutting through farms and family land that took generations to build. His response to a crisis he helped create has been a bill to study the problem, not fix it.

Dear Peter, As I look across the country and see the incredible support building for our team, I wanted to pause for a quiet moment and write to you directly.I don’t know where I would be without supporters like you.Grassroots campaigns have always been about people coming together to stand up for our common values, regardless of state lines. Your support means more to me than I can fully express. Whether you’ve chipped in a few dollars, shared our message, spoken to your friends, or simply kept us in your thoughts, you are the heartbeat of this team. In a race with so much focus, noise, and pressure, knowing you are standing with me gives me the strength to keep fighting every single day for our shared principles, our communities, and the future of our country.You deserve to hear this today: I see your dedication, I never take your commitment for granted, and I am deeply honored to serve as your voice in Washington.Thank you for your trust, your kindness, and your unwavering belief in what we can achieve together.A short email is not enough to express my gratitude for your contribution to our team, so I ask you to read my full note.

On Wednesday, Meta [agreed to pay roughly $18 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/10ec99f0-43b8-4d60-a2f1-b26185d9c56d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to settle claims from 29 states that Facebook and Instagram were built to hook children and hold them there. Fifty-two attorneys general signed on. The deal landed one day into the testimony of Instagram head Adam Mosseri (which California's attorney general called telling).
**Meta admitted no wrongdoing.**
Within hours, people who spent the last two years calling Meta the most predatory corporation in America were posting victory laps. Same accounts, same week. Monday it's a company that sexualizes your daughter for ad revenue. Wednesday it's a "partner in child safety."
And most of those same people are still out there stumping for the _App Store Accountability Act_ , which happens to be the policy Meta has spent more money chasing than any other.
Bottom line: _you 're being played._
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/635beb3a-29fa-45c0-a9c4-d28c30242588?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Meta didn't end up in that Oakland courtroom over one bad quarter.
[Court filings unsealed last November](https://substack.com/redirect/51feea6e-9c67-4e9c-a0aa-31be7752b503?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) allege the company knew millions of adult strangers were contacting minors on its platforms, knew its products made teen mental health worse, and knew that material involving eating disorders, suicide, and child sexual abuse was detected constantly and removed rarely. According to that same brief, none of it was disclosed to the public or to Congress.
A few months before that, Reuters obtained an internal Meta policy document, which the company confirmed was authentic, showing that Meta's own written rules [permitted its AI chatbots to engage a child in romantic or sensual conversation](https://substack.com/redirect/c85268fd-249f-45e5-9900-deb86e48ef5c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Legal approved it. Policy approved it. The chief ethicist approved it. The language came out after a reporter started asking questions, not before.
A New Mexico jury hit the company for [close to $1 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/10ec99f0-43b8-4d60-a2f1-b26185d9c56d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) earlier this year in a separate child exploitation case, and Meta also lost another suit brought by a single teenager. When this trial opened in August, California's deputy attorney general [summed up the business model in four verbs](https://substack.com/redirect/7b692331-a4cc-40f6-81fc-e34b005a786b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): _**hook, hold, harvest, hide.**_
Through every bit of it, Meta denied, delayed, and paid other people to make its arguments in public.
Which brings us to Wednesday.
### Here's what Meta actually agreed to
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ded0e38e-780d-4b85-a9a8-97e2b1c169bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
1. Teen accounts get a two-hour default daily limit and a nudge every 15 minutes to ["encourage intentional use."](https://substack.com/redirect/69e8cfe2-3ed3-4efc-9644-1cab0870701a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
2. Accounts Meta identifies as belonging to minors get locked out overnight between midnight and 6 a.m., with notifications muted from 8 a.m. to 3 p.m. during school.
3. [Like counts disappear](https://substack.com/redirect/10ec99f0-43b8-4d60-a2f1-b26185d9c56d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from teen posts by default, extreme makeup filters are blocked, autoplay can be switched off, and a teen can pick a feed that isn't ranked by the algorithm.
4. An independent auditor checks the work, and Meta is bound to it for ten years.

That's the platform being held responsible (which makes sense).
_But then there 's the rest of it._
Meta pays 70% of the settlement fund to the states in annual installments over the decade. The [other 30% gets paid only if YouTube and TikTok](https://substack.com/redirect/10ec99f0-43b8-4d60-a2f1-b26185d9c56d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) also agree to pay the states and make similar changes to their own apps.
Which is why Meta is now [running full-page newspaper ads](https://substack.com/redirect/69e8cfe2-3ed3-4efc-9644-1cab0870701a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) urging its two biggest competitors to adopt the design rules it just agreed to (the ads leave out the part where a lawsuit made Meta do it).
_**So the punishment doubles as a marketing campaign, an industry standard Meta gets to claim it authored, and a coupon redeemable if the competition folds.**_
Set that against [more than $200 billion in 2025 revenue](https://substack.com/redirect/10ec99f0-43b8-4d60-a2f1-b26185d9c56d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), spread it across ten years, subtract the contingent third, and honestly it's hard to know whether to call the structuring impressive or grotesque.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7c4510d3-36c1-4f1e-a3e8-97d6057bf778?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
### Read the announcement again
In the same statement where Meta said it was ["investing in even stronger technology"](https://substack.com/redirect/10ec99f0-43b8-4d60-a2f1-b26185d9c56d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to catch teens lying about their age, the company called on app stores to help with "age verification."
Same day. Same press release. Meta agreed to write the largest child safety settlement check in the industry's history and used the podium to argue that _somebody else should be running the age checks (i.e. the device manufacturers)._
That wasn't an accident. Meta's been running this play for years, and the App Store Accountability Act is where it pays off.
The bill is the ask...
[S.1586](https://substack.com/redirect/defab1a3-6939-4e15-8b2d-3f77bab9bb4c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and its House companion (not to mention all the state-level bills where they've tried this) do four things: verify age at the app store account level, require parental approval for every download and in-app purchase, make developers assign and justify age ratings, and turn enforcement over to the FTC and the state attorneys general.
_**But none of that touches what Instagram serves a 14-year-old at 11 p.m.**_
It doesn't reach the recommendation engine, or the eating disorder content the plaintiffs say Meta detected and left up. The bill governs the moment of download and then stops, which is roughly where Meta's product begins.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/42ca7714-8fe3-4686-8421-e783e43476b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
What it does do is move the verification cost, the data liability, and the lawsuits onto device manufacturers, while handing Meta a defense it can use in every case that follows where they say something like: "Mom approved the download, so whatever the algorithm served Billy afterward is a family matter."
_**If Meta is the arsonist, this bill inspects the matches.**_
And Meta's fingerprints are all over it...
Bloomberg [reported in July 2025](https://substack.com/redirect/e8b9edef-54a6-4f09-84f3-c0019f8e3713?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Meta was helping fund the Digital Childhood Alliance, the coalition running the state-by-state campaign for app store age verification. That's the same coalition behind the 88% parental support figure that shows up in [the bill's own rollout materials](https://substack.com/redirect/0dad2d8a-de51-443b-b42d-70d595e8acb7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). When a member of Congress reads that number into the record, he's citing research commissioned by a group underwritten by the one company his bill leaves alone.
Meanwhile Meta spent [$26.29 million on federal lobbying in 2025](https://substack.com/redirect/7a95ba07-09f2-46a7-89ce-d18f39eb4db6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (a company record) and [nearly $6 million in the second quarter of 2026](https://substack.com/redirect/664cc02b-4987-4bbf-90ed-c4dcffba6be2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), more than any other tech company in the country.
_**Nobody spends that kind of money to get regulated. You spend it to choose who gets regulated instead.**_
So when someone posts the whistleblower headlines on Tuesday, applauds the settlement on Wednesday, and stumps for the App Store Accountability Act on Thursday, principle isn't the thread running through those three days. Meta got what it wanted on all of them, and Thursday didn't cost a dime.
"Kids cannot consent," Congressman John James [said when he introduced the House version](https://substack.com/redirect/0dad2d8a-de51-443b-b42d-70d595e8acb7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). He's right about that.
So why does his bill let the company whose own guidelines permitted romantic roleplay with minors walk away with paperwork filed by somebody else?
### The part of the settlement nobody is reading
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/582c7b1c-b786-4926-b6db-09adb0801254?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Every protection in that deal rests on three words: accounts identified as minors.
Identified how?
Meta now has to determine which of its users are children, sort them into age brackets, and enforce the restrictions it negotiated with 52 state officials, every day, for ten years. Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers said in open court that compliance here remained "complicated," which is judicial-speak for nobody has worked out how this is supposed to function.
_**Because[age assurance mostly doesn't work](https://substack.com/redirect/69e8cfe2-3ed3-4efc-9644-1cab0870701a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**_****
The available options are behavioral profiling that guesses a user's age from activity and misfires in both directions, a government ID upload, or a face scan. Alexis Ingber (a Syracuse professor who studies this) said the settlement's design changes look fine on paper and depend completely on age verification technology that isn't effective yet.
Translation: the weakest piece of the system is carrying all the weight.
Now stack the App Store Accountability Act on top, pushing that same verification down into the operating system where any app can query it. Every adult in the country holding up a driver's license to prove they aren't 15. [Australia shipped the operating system version in December](https://substack.com/redirect/fc3da8fd-92db-41d4-8e11-fe67cc5cc62f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), sold as "protecting children" and delivered as biometric checks on the entire adult population. Their prime minister predicted it would "reverberate around the world."
He's probably right, and that's the problem.
### Where that leaves parents
Look at where you personally end up in this arrangement. A corporation decides how old your child is. A corporation watches what your child does. An agreement between that corporation and 52 state officials sets the range of choices your family is permitted to make, and you pick from the menu.
We're not asking the government to raise our kids. We're asking it to put the burden on the party that built the harm, and to stop constructing an identity checkpoint for 340 million people on the way there.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8273716e-2671-49bf-b1e8-26dff9bec1fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The pitch never changes...
Either children stay unprotected, or everyone submits to more surveillance. Pick one.
_We reject this false dichotomy._
Children deserve protection from addictive design and corporate exploitation, and they deserve privacy. Parents deserve real tools and genuine authority, not a system where Big Tech determines their kids' ages, monitors their activity, and permits families to choose from a government-approved list.
Holding Meta accountable is necessary. Building a new surveillance infrastructure is not. Two different projects, and Meta has spent about $26 million a year making sure you can't tell them apart.
They didn't lose on Wednesday. They bought ten years, a press cycle, a weapon to use on their competitors, and applause from people who should know better.
Don't hand them the bill too.

name: Mike Rogers
subject: Friend, please keep this between us.

body:
I’m trusting you with something important.

| | Mike Rogers for U.S. Senate
---
|
---
Friend,
---
This is Mike.
---
I am absolutely shaken. Leadership shared something with me - something devastating - and I can't talk about it openly.
