_Story by Raj Patel and Jim Goodman_
Today's data center proponents argue that such projects bring needed jobs and a boost to local economies. Rural America has heard confident pitches like these before. Nearly 40 years ago, concentrated animal feeding operations ([CAFOs](https://substack.com/redirect/ee7a92a6-8fee-493d-82dd-7747539fea15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)) arrived one barn at a time with bold promises of jobs and a county tax base.
By the time neighbors organized, right-to-farm laws and state preemption had cut the ground from under them. All the while, manure lagoons leached into the groundwater and fouled the air, shortening the life expectancy of the farmworkers and downwind neighbors.
Organizing still won real victories, to be sure, from North Carolina's[ CAFO moratorium](https://substack.com/redirect/bb193715-3ee8-4ce3-be83-eb023a4aa274?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 1997 to[ Chris Jones's clean-water campaign](https://substack.com/redirect/0b0e6bf1-1a4a-4878-980a-24d91140ad8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for agriculture secretary in Iowa today. When it comes to CAFOs, the lessons came late, but in the age of artificial intelligence, those same lessons can give rural communities a leg up.
While CAFOs crept into rural America, data centers are arriving as a land rush. This speed is both terrifying and an advantage.[ Texas alone has some 248 proposed data center projects,](https://substack.com/redirect/ac24396f-9fd6-44d0-a673-4549139e7cea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) even though[ 56% of Texans tell pollsters](https://substack.com/redirect/9b755886-e68e-46e9-9099-6a7689f05db6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) they do not want one nearby, which means that rural communities are now asking questions before the deals are locked in. According to the Pew Research Center, of the more than 1,500 data centers proposed or under development,[ 67% are in rural communities](https://substack.com/redirect/725945df-dcaa-4940-a6c6-fca6e516171c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The ultimate question will be: Do rural residents have the power to say no?
The answer is playing out across the country. In November 2025, 800 people filled a board meeting to oppose a billion-dollar Meta-linked project in Howell Township, Michigan, and the developer[ withdrew](https://substack.com/redirect/0ac2bbf7-d9ac-4053-a925-aeb288e409da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). In February,[ the city council of San Marcos, Texas, rejected a $1.5 billion campus](https://substack.com/redirect/0c920eaf-9035-45f5-b834-cdad83df6339?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after nearly nine hours of public comment, then became the first[ Texas city to ban data centers](https://substack.com/redirect/212bd580-cfe4-4b94-8e27-5feede6fb8f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) through its zoning code. Fort Worth is[ drafting](https://substack.com/redirect/391a93d7-3453-4d6f-bd2a-65dde4a8a373?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) data center zoning rules of its own.
Nationally, the poorest census tracts resist data center projects at[ five times the rate of the richest](https://substack.com/redirect/4897f11c-fde3-4896-b744-009fe158f288?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Projects that meet resistance are[ cancelled at several times t](https://substack.com/redirect/1f75e5ff-0b6f-477d-8f30-fbb476910897?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)he rate of those that do not. One[ tracker](https://substack.com/redirect/d962a6c4-def9-42ad-a244-a67d7a886af6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) counts tens of billions of dollars in blocked or delayed projects.
Opposition to data center projects is one of the few issues that many Americans agree on. A[ June Reuters/Ipsos poll](https://substack.com/redirect/4f5a9e0b-85dd-4b28-9c9c-8ee616b6c4c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found that only 14% of respondents would support a data center being built in their community. On July 18, organizers held 142 protests across 42 states in the[ first nationwide protest against data centers](https://substack.com/redirect/f8903c3f-95b3-4078-91a5-eed71d8995e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and artificial intelligence.
Data center hyperscalers are copying the CAFO playbook as best they can. West Virginia has[ stripped its counties](https://substack.com/redirect/e073b286-d050-4989-b09d-7a88690bb11c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and towns of the power to regulate data centers; similarly, the state's[ right-to-farm law](https://substack.com/redirect/d18e6563-3c2d-4832-9492-7e2962d5f073?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) prohibits local governments from bringing civil or criminal action against an agricultural operation as long as it meets state and federal laws, permits, and regulations. When Hill County, Texas, passed the state's first county moratorium in May, a developer sued for $100 million and the county[ rescinded](https://substack.com/redirect/7d1d137e-862f-40a0-8cc3-3d0ae718ecec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) within a week, because Texas counties can zone against neither a data center nor a feedlot. Hood County[ pulled](https://substack.com/redirect/140df6a7-d3aa-407d-ae06-145425e6bae6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its own moratorium after state Sen. Paul Bettencourt (R-Houston) asked whether counties even hold that power; the same senator[ calls](https://substack.com/redirect/212bd580-cfe4-4b94-8e27-5feede6fb8f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the San Marcos ban illegal.
Right-wing organizations like the American Legislative Exchange Council (ALEC), behind the pro-CAFO model legislation of[ right-to-farm laws](https://substack.com/redirect/9f951c17-f857-41b4-9d94-dd59056260fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) since the 1990s, likewise appear intent on denying local control in the data center buildout. At its annual meeting in July, ALEC[ considered a model legislative framework](https://substack.com/redirect/1021662e-ae3c-49ee-93af-157174a13dc0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that would undercut local bans and moratoriums and give data centers the "clear authority to secure power...subject only to objective safety and interconnection standards," as the Center for Media and Democracy[ reported](https://substack.com/redirect/1021662e-ae3c-49ee-93af-157174a13dc0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The meeting featured speakers from Google and Nvidia, along with a Meta sponsorship.
The outburst of anti-data center sentiment ahead of the midterms has forced political leaders to reckon with the issue of local control. This is where data centers and CAFOs diverge. In June, Texas Republican Gov. Greg Abbott, who once hailed Texas as "the epicenter of AI development," called for a[ ban on AI data centers in rural neighborhoods](https://substack.com/redirect/c20c0fee-5e27-4477-b1b1-317c5c155ad6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and a cut to their billion-dollar-a-year tax exemption after facing rare bipartisan pressure. Florida Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a law to[ preserve local control](https://substack.com/redirect/cfc24bc4-160f-4579-990a-a7c1529b6a77?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) over data centers. Michigan's candidates for governor are[ split](https://substack.com/redirect/0e30b60e-fc35-4334-9a5e-a45c0dba7288?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) over the server halls sprouting between Lansing and Detroit. Illinois recently reversed course on its data center policy,[ reeling in the subsidies it had rolled out](https://substack.com/redirect/3f0b125a-dfca-4656-a4da-dfcda24ad85f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2019. And in July, New York became the first state in the nation to enact a one-year moratorium.
So, who hasn't been able to say no? We pulled the locations of CAFOs and data centers in North Carolina and Texas, where the data is easily available, and--yes--got Claude to plot it for us against[ demographic](https://substack.com/redirect/707b90fd-2217-4696-b760-7930cf28dcd1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and[ county boundaries](https://substack.com/redirect/a3e09ea1-dcfc-4525-a66d-88cc2e83350a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

CAFOs, data centers, and race by county in North Carolina.
In North Carolina the answer is pretty clear. The state's 2,482 permitted animal operations cluster in the Black Belt coastal plain where the epidemiologist[ Steve Wing found hog lagoons a generation ago](https://substack.com/redirect/ff4ce646-2c77-4647-a8a9-fdf117a6892b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Weighted by the number of permits each county holds, those counties are 46% people of color, against 34% across North Carolina's hundred counties as a whole. Duplin County alone holds over[ 500 permits](https://substack.com/redirect/2a2bfa3f-aed6-40aa-8d96-9348fbe73677?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and[ 2.2 million allowable hogs](https://substack.com/redirect/3f73df83-c449-4fee-b2ac-f26f4cf88099?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a county where almost half the population of 49,000 are people of color.
Data centers are the inverse of CAFOs. The state's data centers sit in counties whiter than the state average, in the Piedmont towns that lost their historic furniture and textile businesses as well as in wealthy Wake and Mecklenburg counties (respectively home to large cities Raleigh and Charlotte). Two of the state's suspended projects are in adjacent Edgecombe County and Pitt County, where residents informed their resistance based on their history fighting CAFOs.
In 1995, residents of predominantly Black Kingsboro, in Edgecombe County, successfully[ blocked](https://substack.com/redirect/181684ec-3184-4b51-9225-881adef2486c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a major meatpacker from building a 300-acre slaughterhouse in their backyard through efforts to rezone land. When a $19 billion,[ 400-acre data center](https://substack.com/redirect/24459a6d-5640-459a-a59e-5756216c7c2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) came knocking three decades later, residents opposed it en masse. The developer Energy Storage Solutions withdrew its proposal in July, and by August Edgecombe County enacted a two-year moratorium.
In Texas the pattern is a little more complex. Rural Texas tends to be whiter than a state average balanced by majority-Hispanic cities. Yet the feedlot Panhandle is majority-Hispanic meatpacking country, with counties like Deaf Smith and Castro where the workforce lives beside the feedyards it staffs. The rural counties now hosting data centers likewise run less white than rural Texas as a whole.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a2460128-b27b-4259-9b3f-69fe0a108ee0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

The Stargate Oracle AI data center campus in Abilene, Texas. The Stargate Oracle AI data center will span roughly 4 million square feet and will be operated by Oracle for OpenAI. Photo by Brandon Bell/Getty Images.
Other outlier cases in the U.S.: the[ world's densest data center cluster is outside Washington, D.C., in Loudoun County](https://substack.com/redirect/2c5f0ea5-4072-43b8-a084-2b1aa294105f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Virginia, among the wealthiest counties in America, while[ xAI's Colossus runs beside Boxtown,](https://substack.com/redirect/fb1be22d-f3ad-4887-b9fa-e24bb812b3ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a majority-Black neighborhood in Memphis.
The patterning and the possibilities for asking questions about data centers are very different. CAFOs were put next to the disempowered by history. In most of the counties with proposed data centers, there's no local billionaire hyperscaler whose family has been on the land for generations to champion the project, with the historical ability to make people of color, in particular, suffer the consequences in the ways that CAFOs had.
In contrast, data centers are being aimed by site selectors in a hurry, looking for cheap land and water, cheap power, and thin resistance. But they don't have their local defenders and hands on the levers of power in the ways that CAFOs do.
Race and class are the oldest American proxies for who can, and who can't, say no. Here are the questions that constituents can ask their local governments about new data center projects:
### **1\. About water**
Does the permit say the cooling loop is closed, with maximum gallons per day, public metering and penalties? We have yet to find a binding closed-loop commitment in any permit. Who owns the aquifer data, and who pays for the test wells?
### **2\. About power**
Electric cooperatives, unique to rural America, have long been a way for farmers and rural people to claw back some power over their destiny. These cooperatives were established with a "duty to serve" the areas that investor-owned utilities refused to serve because the load factors were low. By pooling their demand, cooperatives could connect their members to a grid and lower their prices.
In the age of artificial intelligence, public utilities--rural electric cooperatives included--face a dilemma. The more a cooperative buys from its wholesale supplier, the greater its load factor and therefore the lower the cooperative's average cost of power. When a data center project fields new requests for power, it can be life changing. Having a client with a reliable 24/7 demand for electricity means a predictable increase in the co-op's load factor. All that new volume could, in principle, make every member's bill cheaper and bring new system upgrades. It's tempting to shut up and take the deal.
But as with any gift horse, every farmer knows to check the teeth. Data centers often have greater access to capital than their would-be electric cooperative providers, and their rise as buyers means a shift in the balance of bargaining power in the marketplace. Will attitudes toward universal service obligations remain in place? Will consumer protection policies evolve? And which regulator should be responsible for developing and overseeing new industry guardrails?
Who pays for the substation and the lines? Port Washington, Wisconsin, found itself on the[ hook for a $90 million substation it did not need](https://substack.com/redirect/df505330-8fc2-4c41-b4f2-360a730d43d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Is there a curtailment agreement[ cutting the data center first in a grid emergency](https://substack.com/redirect/aec758e0-6c7d-45f0-8690-fb9f2dc7e258?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), as Texas now requires of loads over 75 megawatts? Are residential rates fenced off in a separate rate class? And for rural electric cooperative members: Does the all-requirements wholesale contract cap the solar and wind members may build, and would a giant new load deepen that dependence? Why do big loads get lower per kilowatt prices as they increase their usage while conservation earns nothing? Will data centers inherit the same pricing structure?
### **3\. About money**
What does each abatement cost per permanent job, when a hyperscale facility employs a few dozen people? Will advance payments be required to pay for infrastructure upgrades? Will they accept provisions for interruptible power during times of peak demand to prevent rolling blackouts? Are there clawbacks? Is there a decommissioning bond for the day the hardware is scrap, as we now demand of wind farms?
### **4\. About democracy**
Did any utility or government official sign a non-disclosure agreement (NDA)? Can our county or township legally say no, and if not, which law took the power and who voted for it?
Everything CAFO country learned, it learned too late, after the wells were ruined, after the smell lowered adjacent property values and health outcomes, after the statutes were written. Data centers are arriving early enough that the questions can still be asked in time, even as the hyperscalers[ find friends in Washington, D.C](https://substack.com/redirect/55f6b242-c50a-46ff-b17b-5db7b2675167?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)., and in statehouses around the country, who'll say yes to them so that local communities won't be able to say no.
If we want to prevent Amazon, Meta, and OpenAI from**** riding roughshod over our communities and land, it will be because average people, urban and rural alike, have joined forces to stop the trillionaire class from building their wealth off our backs.

clean_body: From CAFOs to data centers, corporate America dodges local control. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more From CAFOs to data centers, corporate America dodges local control. | | | Aug 27 | | | | | | | | | | | | This piece by Raj Patel, a research professor at the Lyndon B. Johnson School of Public Affairs and a member of the International Panel of Experts on Sustainable Food Systems, and Jim Goodman, a retired dairy farmer, looks at the way hyperscalers are approaching the construction of data centers in rural communities and the rights those communities have. The piece is part of Drop Site's ongoing collaboration with Barn Raiser to put a focus on rural politics with a newsletter running through November. | | ---|---|--- Donna Hull stakes a "no data center" signs on her property's fence line next to the proposed Crusoe data center in Jewett, Texas. Photo by Antranik Tavitian/for The Washington Post via Getty Images. Story by Raj Patel and Jim Goodman Today's data center proponents argue that such projects bring needed jobs and a boost to local economies. Rural America has heard confident pitches like these before. Nearly 40 years ago, concentrated animal feeding operations () arrived one barn at a time with bold promises of jobs and a county tax base. By the time neighbors organized, right-to-farm laws and state preemption had cut the ground from under them. All the while, manure lagoons leached into the groundwater and fouled the air, shortening the life expectancy of the farmworkers and downwind neighbors. Organizing still won real victories, to be sure, from North Carolina's in 1997 to for agriculture secretary in Iowa today. When it comes to CAFOs, the lessons came late, but in the age of artificial intelligence, those same lessons can give rural communities a leg up. While CAFOs crept into rural America, data centers are arriving as a land rush. This speed is both terrifying and an advantage. even though they do not want one nearby, which means that rural communities are now asking questions before the deals are locked in. According to the Pew Research Center, of the more than 1,500 data centers proposed or under development,. The ultimate question will be: Do rural residents have the power to say no? The answer is playing out across the country. In November 2025, 800 people filled a board meeting to oppose a billion-dollar Meta-linked project in Howell Township, Michigan, and the developer. In February, after nearly nine hours of public comment, then became the first through its zoning code. Fort Worth is data center zoning rules of its own. Nationally, the poorest census tracts resist data center projects at. Projects that meet resistance are rate of those that do not. One counts tens of billions of dollars in blocked or delayed projects. Opposition to data center projects is one of the few issues that many Americans agree on. A found that only 14% of respondents would support a data center being built in their community. On July 18, organizers held 142 protests across 42 states in the and artificial intelligence. Data center hyperscalers are copying the CAFO playbook as best they can. West Virginia has and towns of the power to regulate data centers; similarly, the state's prohibits local governments from bringing civil or criminal action against an agricultural operation as long as it meets state and federal laws, permits, and regulations. When Hill County, Texas, passed the state's first county moratorium in May, a developer sued for $100 million and the county within a week, because Texas counties can zone against neither a data center nor a feedlot. Hood County its own moratorium after state Sen. Paul Bettencourt (R-Houston) asked whether counties even hold that power; the same senator the San Marcos ban illegal. Right-wing organizations like the American Legislative Exchange Council (ALEC), behind the pro-CAFO model legislation of since the 1990s, likewise appear intent on denying local control in the data center buildout. At its annual meeting in July, ALEC that would undercut local bans and moratoriums and give data centers the "clear authority to secure power...subject only to objective safety and interconnection standards," as the Center for Media and Democracy. The meeting featured speakers from Google and Nvidia, along with a Meta sponsorship. The outburst of anti-data center sentiment ahead of the midterms has forced political leaders to reckon with the issue of local control. This is where data centers and CAFOs diverge. In June, Texas Republican Gov. Greg Abbott, who once hailed Texas as "the epicenter of AI development," called for a and a cut to their billion-dollar-a-year tax exemption after facing rare bipartisan pressure. Florida Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a law to over data centers. Michigan's candidates for governor are over the server halls sprouting between Lansing and Detroit. Illinois recently reversed course on its data center policy, in 2019. And in July, New York became the first state in the nation to enact a one-year moratorium. So, who hasn't been able to say no? We pulled the locations of CAFOs and data centers in North Carolina and Texas, where the data is easily available, and--yes--got Claude to plot it for us against and. | | ---|---|--- CAFOs, data centers, and race by county in Texas. | | ---|---|--- CAFOs, data centers, and race by county in North Carolina. In North Carolina the answer is pretty clear. The state's 2,482 permitted animal operations cluster in the Black Belt coastal plain where the epidemiologist. Weighted by the number of permits each county holds, those counties are 46% people of color, against 34% across North Carolina's hundred counties as a whole. Duplin County alone holds over and in a county where almost half the population of 49,000 are people of color. Data centers are the inverse of CAFOs. The state's data centers sit in counties whiter than the state average, in the Piedmont towns that lost their historic furniture and textile businesses as well as in wealthy Wake and Mecklenburg counties (respectively home to large cities Raleigh and Charlotte). Two of the state's suspended projects are in adjacent Edgecombe County and Pitt County, where residents informed their resistance based on their history fighting CAFOs. In 1995, residents of predominantly Black Kingsboro, in Edgecombe County, successfully a major meatpacker from building a 300-acre slaughterhouse in their backyard through efforts to rezone land. When a $19 billion, came knocking three decades later, residents opposed it en masse. The developer Energy Storage Solutions withdrew its proposal in July, and by August Edgecombe County enacted a two-year moratorium. In Texas the pattern is a little more complex. Rural Texas tends to be whiter than a state average balanced by majority-Hispanic cities. Yet the feedlot Panhandle is majority-Hispanic meatpacking country, with counties like Deaf Smith and Castro where the workforce lives beside the feedyards it staffs. The rural counties now hosting data centers likewise run less white than rural Texas as a whole. | | ---|---|--- The Stargate Oracle AI data center campus in Abilene, Texas. The Stargate Oracle AI data center will span roughly 4 million square feet and will be operated by Oracle for OpenAI. Photo by Brandon Bell/Getty Images. Other outlier cases in the U.S.: the, Virginia, among the wealthiest counties in America, while a majority-Black neighborhood in Memphis. The patterning and the possibilities for asking questions about data centers are very different. CAFOs were put next to the disempowered by history. In most of the counties with proposed data centers, there's no local billionaire hyperscaler whose family has been on the land for generations to champion the project, with the historical ability to make people of color, in particular, suffer the consequences in the ways that CAFOs had. In contrast, data centers are being aimed by site selectors in a hurry, looking for cheap land and water, cheap power, and thin resistance. But they don't have their local defenders and hands on the levers of power in the ways that CAFOs do. Race and class are the oldest American proxies for who can, and who can't, say no. Here are the questions that constituents can ask their local governments about new data center projects: 1\. About water Does the permit say the cooling loop is closed, with maximum gallons per day, public metering and penalties? We have yet to find a binding closed-loop commitment in any permit. Who owns the aquifer data, and who pays for the test wells? 2\. About power Electric cooperatives, unique to rural America, have long been a way for farmers and rural people to claw back some power over their destiny. These cooperatives were established with a "duty to serve" the areas that investor-owned utilities refused to serve because the load factors were low. By pooling their demand, cooperatives could connect their members to a grid and lower their prices. In the age of artificial intelligence, public utilities--rural electric cooperatives included--face a dilemma. The more a cooperative buys from its wholesale supplier, the greater its load factor and therefore the lower the cooperative's average cost of power. When a data center project fields new requests for power, it can be life changing. Having a client with a reliable 24/7 demand for electricity means a predictable increase in the co-op's load factor. All that new volume could, in principle, make every member's bill cheaper and bring new system upgrades. It's tempting to shut up and take the deal. But as with any gift horse, every farmer knows to check the teeth. Data centers often have greater access to capital than their would-be electric cooperative providers, and their rise as buyers means a shift in the balance of bargaining power in the marketplace. Will attitudes toward universal service obligations remain in place? Will consumer protection policies evolve? And which regulator should be responsible for developing and overseeing new industry guardrails? Who pays for the substation and the lines? Port Washington, Wisconsin, found itself on the. Is there a curtailment agreement, as Texas now requires of loads over 75 megawatts? Are residential rates fenced off in a separate rate class? And for rural electric cooperative members: Does the all-requirements wholesale contract cap the solar and wind members may build, and would a giant new load deepen that dependence? Why do big loads get lower per kilowatt prices as they increase their usage while conservation earns nothing? Will data centers inherit the same pricing structure? 3\. About money What does each abatement cost per permanent job, when a hyperscale facility employs a few dozen people? Will advance payments be required to pay for infrastructure upgrades? Will they accept provisions for interruptible power during times of peak demand to prevent rolling blackouts? Are there clawbacks? Is there a decommissioning bond for the day the hardware is scrap, as we now demand of wind farms? 4\. About democracy Did any utility or government official sign a non-disclosure agreement (NDA)? Can our county or township legally say no, and if not, which law took the power and who voted for it? Everything CAFO country learned, it learned too late, after the wells were ruined, after the smell lowered adjacent property values and health outcomes, after the statutes were written. Data centers are arriving early enough that the questions can still be asked in time, even as the hyperscalers., and in statehouses around the country, who'll say yes to them so that local communities won't be able to say no. If we want to prevent Amazon, Meta, and OpenAI from** riding roughshod over our communities and land, it will be because average people, urban and rural alike, have joined forces to stop the trillionaire class from building their wealth off our backs. body:
My community showed me what's possible.

When I was a kid, reading this kind of headline would have been unimaginable: [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138045116/642789532/724725427?amounts=10,15,25,50,75,100,250&refcode=email_082726_pappas-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjOWJlMTRiMy00NmEyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTliZWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=nj5FB4KKnKymqCCqJBcZg7U7eXsw3kM52xK4zhOA9G0=) Growing up as a gay person in New Hampshire, I never imagined I could live out — let alone run for U.S. Senate. **But my community showed me what's possible.** You helped me win _four times_ in one of the most competitive congressional districts in the country. We’ve made tremendous progress since I was younger. But there’s still something we’ve never done. **We’ve never elected a gay man to the Senate.** To be clear, I’m not running for Senate just to make history. I’m in this race for the people of New Hampshire – **_all of us._** But the prospect of moving the needle of progress forward is deeply meaningful to me. This is an opportunity for representation in the Senate. It’s also important that LGBTQ+ people have more seats at the table at a time when our rights are coming under attack. **We can win this election for the people of New Hampshire, charting a path forward for our shared future – and we can tear down barriers and make history at the same time.** [Will you split a $25 contribution between my campaign and John Hickenlooper right now to stand with me in this historic fight?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138045118/642789533/724725427?amounts=10,15,25,50,75,100,250&refcode=email_082726_pappas-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjOWJlMTRiMy00NmEyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTliZWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=nj5FB4KKnKymqCCqJBcZg7U7eXsw3kM52xK4zhOA9G0=) **Thank you for supporting me in this campaign.** No matter who you are, who you love, who you pray to, or where you're from — know that I'll always have your back. With gratitude, Chris

clean_body: My community showed me what's possible. When I was a kid, reading this kind of headline would have been unimaginable: = Growing up as a gay person in New Hampshire, I never imagined I could live out — let alone run for U.S. Senate. But my community showed me what's possible. You helped me win four times in one of the most competitive congressional districts in the country. We’ve made tremendous progress since I was younger. But there’s still something we’ve never done. We’ve never elected a gay man to the Senate. To be clear, I’m not running for Senate just to make history. I’m in this race for the people of New Hampshire – all of us. But the prospect of moving the needle of progress forward is deeply meaningful to me. This is an opportunity for representation in the Senate. It’s also important that LGBTQ+ people have more seats at the table at a time when our rights are coming under attack. We can win this election for the people of New Hampshire, charting a path forward for our shared future – and we can tear down barriers and make history at the same time. = Thank you for supporting me in this campaign. Folks might've killed to have my job.
I was a sideline reporter for pro football and basketball. I covered some of the most exciting games in history. I watched sports for a living. And I loved every minute, every touchdown, and every Hail Mary.
I reached the pinnacle of my career... but there was one problem:
I had to watch what I said. I was a public-facing representative for a world-class sports network. I couldn't share everything I believed, and no one really knew I was a Conservative.
So I hung up my press badge and quit my dream job so I could speak my mind.

**People said I was OUT OF MY MIND. **
**But I knew God was leading me in a certain direction, and that 's no time for half-measures. I knew he had a plan for my life. So I took a leap of faith and never looked back.**

**I believe Minnesota is the land of 10,000 problems right now. **
**And I believe a no-BS, sane person who 's ALL-IN can win this seat. **
**But I 'd be lying if I said fundraising doesn't make a difference in a race like this. The far-Left is readying a FORTUNE to drown out our message and take this seat out of play. **
**Our path to victory solely depends on raising enough to keep up. **
**My finance team tells me we 'll need to bring in donors ASAP so we can: 1) Hire staff, 2) Recruit volunteers in every corner of the state, 3) Print yard signs, 4) Launch our advertising blitz, and 5) Start contacting on-the-fence voters. **

clean_body: This is Michele Tafoya – I’ve got a quick story to share if you’ll indulge me for a few moments. | Hi there, I hope you are well! Folks might've killed to have my job. I was a sideline reporter for pro football and basketball. I covered some of the most exciting games in history. I watched sports for a living. And I loved every minute, every touchdown, and every Hail Mary. I reached the pinnacle of my career... but there was one problem: I had to watch what I said. I was a public-facing representative for a world-class sports network. I couldn't share everything I believed, and no one really knew I was a Conservative. So I hung up my press badge and quit my dream job so I could speak my mind. It was the hardest decision I've ever made. I was scared, excited, and liberated - all at the same time. | | | Oregon didn't just adopt vote-by-mail. We INVENTED it. **So when the US Supreme Court cleared the way for Trump's executive order restricting mail-in ballots yesterday, understand what that means: ** There is no state with more on the line than Oregon. This order isn't aimed at some abstract "voting system." **It's aimed at the way every single Oregonian votes.** Here's what Trump’s USPS order does. It orders the Postal Service to deliver ballots only to voters on a federal list — a list built by THIS administration. Their postmaster already said the quiet part out loud: states that don't hand over their voter data likely won't have mail ballots delivered at all. Now here's what I know. **I'm Oregon's chief elections officer. We have taken this administration to court twice — over their demand for your voter data, and over their first election order. We won both times.** **And now we’ve filed suit again. ** **The Constitution hasn't changed** since then. States run elections. Not presidents. Not postmasters. And this November, Oregon will run the same safe, fair, accurate vote-by-mail election we've run for 25 years — and I will use every power of this office to make sure of it. **[But fighting them in court is just one way of defending our elections. We must have the resources to communicate about what’s at stake — every lawsuit, every rule change, every attempt to rewrite how Oregon votes. That’s why I’m using my campaign to help travel around the state and talk directly to voters too. clean_body: | | | = | | | Oregon didn't just adopt vote-by-mail. We INVENTED it. So when the US Supreme Court cleared the way for Trump's executive order restricting mail-in ballots yesterday, understand what that means: There is no state with more on the line than Oregon. This order isn't aimed at some abstract "voting system." It's aimed at the way every single Oregonian votes. Here's what Trump’s USPS order does. It orders the Postal Service to deliver ballots only to voters on a federal list — a list built by THIS administration. Their postmaster already said the quiet part out loud: states that don't hand over their voter data likely won't have mail ballots delivered at all. Now here's what I know. I'm Oregon's chief elections officer. We have taken this administration to court twice — over their demand for your voter data, and over their first election order. We won both times. And now we’ve filed suit again. The Constitution hasn't changed since then. States run elections. Not presidents. Not postmasters. And this November, Oregon will run the same safe, fair, accurate vote-by-mail election we've run for 25 years — and I will use every power of this office to make sure of it. = = They think they can push around a small state like Oregon. | | | | Back-to-school season is here in West Michigan.
---
For parents, that means new schedules, school supply lists, earlier bedtimes, and trying to remember where everyone is supposed to be in the morning.
But this time of year also reminds me why I do this work.
Our kids are growing up in the communities we're shaping today. They deserve great schools, safe neighborhoods, clean water, good jobs close to home, and an economy where they can afford to build a life of their own someday.
I want West Michigan, and this country, to be a place where families can put down roots and feel hopeful about the future their kids will inherit.

For parents, that means new schedules, school supply lists, earlier bedtimes, and trying to remember where everyone is supposed to be in the morning. But this time of year also reminds me why I do this work. Our kids are growing up in the communities we're shaping today. They deserve great schools, safe neighborhoods, clean water, good jobs close to home, and an economy where they can afford to build a life of their own someday. I want West Michigan, and this country, to be a place where families can put down roots and feel hopeful about the future their kids will inherit. clean_body: I couldn't have done this without you, but we cannot take a day off. We need to look to November. | Thank you, Peter. It's been a long six weeks, but because you were by my side, we won. Your generosity helped us through the Special Election Primary and through a head-to-head runoff. But that was just the first step to securing this seat. I am the first woman United States senator in South Carolina history. My Democratic opponent, Dr. Annie Andrews, cannot be the second. Here's where the race stands. Two statewide elections in less than 6 weeks were expensive. We knew it would be a tough battle - it was. We did not want to leave anything to chance, so we had to ensure every dollar we raised was well spent on television ads, voter contacts, and signs across South Carolina. We are starting at square one, going into the general election, and let me tell you about our Democrat opponent. She's raising millions from liberal donors who want nothing more than to flip this seat and stop President Trump's agenda in Washington. I need your help again, Peter. Now that we're in the general election, we need to compete with the liberal money flooding South Carolina. I hate to ask for your help again, especially when you've been by my side for the last six weeks, but I wouldn't ask if I didn't need it. We won Tuesday night, but that's just the beginning. Let's make sure we win again in November. Thank you, Darline Graham P.S. Thank you for being by my side over the last few weeks. It means so much to me. body:
A socialist endorsement for mayor: What Denver DSA’s backing of Shontel Lewis means.
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends!
Want your full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** Denver's [DSA gave its top endorsement](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to Councilwoman Shontel Lewis' mayoral bid against incumbent Mike Johnston; City Council committed [$5.3 million to a pedestrian bridge](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) linking RTD to the new Summit FC stadium; a [federal judge sided with GEO Group](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) against a state law requiring more detention-facility inspections, ruling it targeted the company's tuberculosis-hit Adams County site; and a Loveland sculptor [gifted a bronze Jefferson statue to the White House Rose Garden](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for the nation's 250th anniversary.
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent [barred illegal immigrants from four federal tax credits](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), citing a 1996 law limiting benefits to citizens and legal residents.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** Fox News' Taylor Budowich says [Democrats are exaggerating AI fears](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to justify government control; American Thinker's Dr. Brian Joondeph argues [open-borders logic collapses](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) without a limiting principle, citing nearly nine million illegal entries under Biden.
This is your Mountain Minute for Thursday, August 27, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[A socialist endorsement for mayor: What Denver DSA’s backing of Shontel Lewis means.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Denver’s Democratic Socialists of America chapter has picked a candidate in the 2027 race for mayor. In an August 25 release, the chapter said it was “proud to announce their endorsement of Councilwoman Shontel M. Lewis for Mayor of Denver in the 2027 election.”
The endorsement comes from the chapter itself, in its own words. What is worth slowing down on is the word itself. For DSA, an endorsement is not a pat on the back. It is a category with rules attached, and the rules are written down.
Lewis is a first-term councilmember for District 8, a seat that runs through Park Hill and parts of East Colfax. She filed an affidavit in July to run for mayor in the April 6, 2027, municipal election, according to the Denver Clerk and Recorder’s Office. She will challenge incumbent Mayor Mike Johnston, who filed for reelection in August.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Judge Finds Key Provision Of Colorado Detention Law Conflicts With Federal Authority](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [THE CENTER SQUARE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_A federal judge sides with a private prison contractor, ruling Colorado's new inspection law improperly targets a facility operating under federal authority._
* **Federal supremacy wins out:** U.S. District Judge Daniel Domenico ruled in favor of GEO Group, finding that Colorado's HB 26-1276 — which mandates increased health and safety inspections at immigration detention facilities — improperly discriminates against GEO based on its status as a federal contractor, citing the Constitution's supremacy clause.
* **A law targeting one facility:** GEO's attorney argued the law was crafted to single out the company's Adams County facility, the state's only immigration detention center, since Colorado law would have imposed inspection costs and fines up to $50,000 for noncompliance.
* **Part of a broader legal pattern:** The ruling comes amid extensive litigation between Colorado and the Trump administration over immigration enforcement — Attorney General Phil Weiser's office has filed or joined 77 such lawsuits — while GEO separately faces a state lawsuit over denying health officials access to investigate a tuberculosis outbreak at the same facility.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|

**ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****[What the Supreme Court did, and did not do, on Trump’s mail-ballot order](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY SHAINA COLE | NATIONAL | AUGUST 25** _The Supreme Court handed the Trump administration a win Monday on mail-in voting, and the headlines said so. But for a Colorado voter, nothing has changed yet. The state remains set to send November ballots under existing rules, because a second court order the justices did not touch still blocks the part of the president’s plan most directly tied to how voters receive their ballots._
__
**[Three federal cases test whether Colorado treats gun rights as policy or as a limit on government](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY C. J. GARBO | COMMENTARY | AUGUST 25** _Colorado has spent more than a generation treating the Second Amendment as a public-policy question. That is the first mistake. The Bill of Rights does not identify subjects upon which government may act whenever legislators believe their intentions are sufficiently benevolent._ ____
__**[DougCo’s charter proposal protects schools from competition, not choice](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY KIM GILMARTIN | COMMENTARY | AUGUST 24** _Douglas County has long been known as a community that values school choice, which is one reason a resolution recently advanced by the Douglas County School District (DCSD) Board of Education deserves much more attention than it has received._**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**__

But if you provide a child with a rotten education, nothing happens, except that you're liable to be given more money to do it with. Well, we've discovered that money alone isn't the answer."_ – Ronald Reagan

| Peter,
My name is Dadrius Lanus. I am the Executive Director of the Louisiana Democratic Party.
Myself and over 600 Louisanans showed up at the Louisiana State Capitol last month to protest MAGA's declaration of a state of emergency that canceled our congressional elections and ultimately eliminated the majority-Black district of Democratic Congressman Cleo Fields (D-LA).
---
| | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001cc3wjVehby4uE4UMSNTFrQx-QzFdsleNIVAHtL36biam-TuMAUlKJvDWRq1A4-XkREQzd3FO21WuBgL148mG0B6ObOtNkbCkhA09Dff9MghVixfXf4MF1OSo95C90se_DbyJijfq5BSxi4Rd8yOdAxUFpOZQRbfpvJoTp0VPkITRzQD9BHJLOKSNUwubPQtTri8O5vRBKhniaSNMVyjuxyIRfdNkq9DG&c=HaKknH1KHtPpJNRh1qnjQsQ-mu0oyM6ynhdSWa7ZXuAM5WoO7sKpRw==&ch=4NgVABgc-t90YsFXS7YrLEGX-ogK50bROJ8KUqXh-ScLxuDEHPm9zQ==)
---
That's me in the gray suit at the State Capitol.
During the hearing, I spoke out against their segregationist gerrymander and Louisiana Republican Senator Jay Morris shouted at me, "Y'all need to shut up, boy."
We all know what he meant by this.
Jay Morris is the same Louisiana senator who passed legislation to eliminate the New Orleans Criminal Clerk of Court seat to prevent a duly elected Black man, Calvin Duncan, from taking office.
When asked why he was so motivated to eliminate Duncan's office, Morris said, "There are many ways to skin a cat around here." Checo Yancy, a Black civil rights leader, astutely responded to Morris saying: "We know what you mean ... white men around here used to say there are many ways to skin a negro."
This senator led the charge to suspend our May 16th Congressional elections and has offered up many ways to carve up Louisiana so every congressional district is majority white.
They can lie through their teeth that voter suppression and seat elimination are not about race, but their racist dog whistles give them away every single time.
[This fight started right here in the Louisiana House, and it's already shaping courts and legislatures across the country. Can you chip in $25, $10, or even just $5 today to help us fight back in Louisiana? ](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001cc3wjVehby4uE4UMSNTFrQx-QzFdsleNIVAHtL36biam-TuMAUlKJvDWRq1A4-XkpHKQVVNb8gTalmnXZTRXMM054ZRkB-B_A7VjA0nylSTGKN6nb1gA02-h3wCT4WyIsg4JothBbWQQfOd6Yden826A8-vG0gmRFj0uKn3LOixQLFPInjG4LgYJD_tuADMDdRT80ww-nvTVFKQdQAGI8MUVMP9wMGE9_pTUY98FKzQ=&c=HaKknH1KHtPpJNRh1qnjQsQ-mu0oyM6ynhdSWa7ZXuAM5WoO7sKpRw==&ch=4NgVABgc-t90YsFXS7YrLEGX-ogK50bROJ8KUqXh-ScLxuDEHPm9zQ==)

Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision.
When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.
Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.
Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.
So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families.
And I've got to tell you, the Washington elite do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don’t even believe us.
They're focused on their own wallets – not ours. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.
It’s why our prices keep rising, while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.
My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.

clean_body: = Hello - My name is Mary Peltola, and after winning an open primary, I am officially running in the general election for United States Senate in Alaska. I want to share with you why I made the decision to run – and to ask for your support as we begin the general election together. = | | = Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision. When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance. Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity. Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find. So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families. And I've got to tell you, the Washington elite do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don’t even believe us. They're focused on their own wallets – not ours. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest. It’s why our prices keep rising, while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted. My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning. But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need to also focus on another priority: fighting the corruption that threatens our very democracy. I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future. This is going to be the closest and most consequential Senate race this year, and I cannot do this alone. clean_body: Four years after Pat Ryan was elected, he has not passed a single bill. | Fellow Patriot, Please take a moment to read this campaign trail update from our team. Jackie was just with Speaker of the House Mike Johnson right here in the Hudson Valley, and the conversation was clear: how do we keep the House red? And what does it take to win NY-18? It was a powerful reminder of what this race means beyond just the Hudson Valley. Flipping NY-18 is a major part of keeping the House red, and Jackie is ready to do her part. This past weekend marked four years since the Hudson Valley sent Pat Ryan to Washington. Four years later, his record as a primary sponsor sits at zero bills passed into law. Not one. He cannot even get a post office renamed. He has gotten richer while everyone else in this district has fallen further behind, abandoned his promise to be an independent centrist, and spent the last year cozying up to the DSA and the radical left to advance his own political future. If Democrats take back the House, Pat Ryan goes back to Washington with them. That means nonstop impeachment attempts against President Trump, defunding ICE and border enforcement, and tax hikes on every working family and small business in this community. Will you chip in today and help flip NY-18? Thank you, Connor, Team Jackie | | Paid for by Jackie Auringer for Congress Don't want to receive any more of our emails? We hate to see you go: .

Friend, We're now a little less than 10 weeks out from Election Day, and that changes how this campaign operates day to day. body:
Angela Gonzales-Torres is exactly the kind of fearless, people-powered leader we were built to back.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260827-1&t=1&akid=3929%2E587540%2Eza-BUC)
Exciting news, Peter:
**Leaders We Deserve is proud to announce we’re endorsing Angela Gonzales-Torres for Congress in California’s 34th Congressional District!**
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260827_1_agt.-Rb2p0&refcode=em20260827-3929&t=2&akid=3929%2E587540%2Eza-BUC)
I’ll tell you more about Angela, but first, this is a critical race for working people in Los Angeles, and she needs our support to win. **[Will you split a $5 contribution between Angela and Leaders We Deserve today?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260827_1_agt.-Rb2p0&refcode=em20260827-3929&amount=5&t=3&akid=3929%2E587540%2Eza-BUC)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260827_1_agt.-Rb2p0&amount=5&refcode=em20260827-3929&t=4&akid=3929%2E587540%2Eza-BUC)**
**Angela Gonzales-Torres** was born and raised in Highland Park. Her father, a military veteran, was deported over a decade ago — so she was raised by a single mother who relied on SNAP and Medicaid just to get by. She knows firsthand the issues working Angelenos are facing right now, because she’s lived them. And she’s spent her entire life turning that lived experience into service, working with people transitioning from prison into universities and fighting for permanent affordable housing.
Angela knows this district personally, and deeply. As President of her Neighborhood Council, in the Los Angeles Mayor's Office, and on Metro's Public Safety Advisory Committee, **she has spent her life fighting alongside her neighbors resisting displacement, in communities carrying the highest costs of incarceration, the dirtiest air in the county, and the most eviction notices in the city.**
In Congress, Angela will fight to get corporate money out of politics, protect tenants from displacement, expand access to permanent affordable housing, co-sponsor Medicare for All, and push for a humane, inclusive approach to immigration. **Angela is exactly the kind of leader CA-34 deserves to reflect the courage of its people.**
Her opponent, incumbent Jimmy Gomez, has taken _millions_ of dollars from AIPAC over his tenure in Congress. He refused to sign onto the original Gaza ceasefire resolution in Congress, and in a district facing a severe housing affordability crisis, he’s taken real estate lobby dollars from the same entities displacing working people in core LA neighborhoods.
**CA-34 deserves leadership that will only ever serve their interests — not leave them behind for whoever's writing the biggest check.**
Leaders We Deserve doesn’t take a single dollar from corporate PACs or special interests — and neither does Angela. Our ability to back candidates like her depends entirely on this grassroots team showing up when it counts.
**[SoPeter , will you split a $5 contribution between Angela and Leaders We Deserve today to help bring real accountability to CA-34?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260827_1_agt.-Rb2p0&refcode=em20260827-3929&amount=5&t=5&akid=3929%2E587540%2Eza-BUC)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

Exciting news, Peter: Leaders We Deserve is proud to announce we’re endorsing Angela Gonzales-Torres for Congress in California’s 34th Congressional District! I’ll tell you more about Angela, but first, this is a critical race for working people in Los Angeles, and she needs our support to win. Angela Gonzales-Torres was born and raised in Highland Park. Her father, a military veteran, was deported over a decade ago — so she was raised by a single mother who relied on SNAP and Medicaid just to get by. She knows firsthand the issues working Angelenos are facing right now, because she’s lived them. And she’s spent her entire life turning that lived experience into service, working with people transitioning from prison into universities and fighting for permanent affordable housing. Angela knows this district personally, and deeply. As President of her Neighborhood Council, in the Los Angeles Mayor's Office, and on Metro's Public Safety Advisory Committee, she has spent her life fighting alongside her neighbors resisting displacement, in communities carrying the highest costs of incarceration, the dirtiest air in the county, and the most eviction notices in the city. In Congress, Angela will fight to get corporate money out of politics, protect tenants from displacement, expand access to permanent affordable housing, co-sponsor Medicare for All, and push for a humane, inclusive approach to immigration. Angela is exactly the kind of leader CA-34 deserves to reflect the courage of its people. Her opponent, incumbent Jimmy Gomez, has taken millions of dollars from AIPAC over his tenure in Congress. He refused to sign onto the original Gaza ceasefire resolution in Congress, and in a district facing a severe housing affordability crisis, he’s taken real estate lobby dollars from the same entities displacing working people in core LA neighborhoods. CA-34 deserves leadership that will only ever serve their interests — not leave them behind for whoever's writing the biggest check. Leaders We Deserve doesn’t take a single dollar from corporate PACs or special interests — and neither does Angela. Our ability to back candidates like her depends entirely on this grassroots team showing up when it counts. Thank you, David Hogg

For generations of American mothers, Heidi Murkoff's _What to Expect When You 're Expecting_ was the first book they bought when they found out they were pregnant. Today, the What To Expect brand has grown to include several books, a website, and an app, but it appears they've also expanded into spreading political propaganda related to the COVID vaccine.

What To Expect's carefully cultivated trust with pregnant women became one of the most effective delivery systems for Anthony Fauci's COVID-19 vaccine messaging related to the vaccine's impact on young children and pregnant women. Hey, there's a little-known loophole that makes it possible to take non-binding ownership of a house...

(and therefore flip it)

\- without putting any money down
\- without having to get a mortgage
\- without taking on any risk

You basically get control of the deed to a house and then transfer it to a new owner all in one day.

Nowhere is this more apparent than in Louisiana where MAGA has used their complete control of state power to declare a 'state of emergency,' launching a full tilt fascist assault unparalleled to anywhere else in the nation.
They've implemented a slate of the most extreme far-right policies in modern US history, they deployed the national guard to New Orleans, rushed through Jim Crow style maps, cancelled our elections, and conducted a coup to eliminate a sitting Democratic US Congressman. We all fear what comes next.
But for every sign of destruction and division, there is something else-- hope for salvation on a biblical scale: The Miracle on the Mississippi.

Hi, it’s Carole King 🎶, and I personally wrote this email.
Congressman Chris Pappas has been representing New Hampshire’s District 1 in the U.S. House of Representatives since 2019 — and now he’s running to serve in the U.S. Senate.
**[Will you contribute whatever you can afford right now? If you can only afford $1, enter $1 in the blank space. Whatever you give, your participation matters!](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260827_2.-ZJF4k&refcode=em20260827-2&t=2&akid=8559%2E582294%2EC87G0D)**
When I first met Chris in New Hampshire, I learned that he was a descendant of Greek immigrants who opened an ice cream shop in Manchester in 1917. Later they expanded the shop into a restaurant that his family still owns.
**Chris Pappas grew up working in the restaurant alongside people who helped each other in times of need.**
Meanwhile his likely Republican opponent has a decades-long history of associating with the super-rich and turning a blind eye to the needs of everyday people.
**Chris sees and hears his constituents, and unlike his opponents, he doesn’t rely on the MAGA billionaire network to fund his campaign.**
**[Will you help Chris beat back the billionaires?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260827_2.-ZJF4k&refcode=em20260827-2&t=3&akid=8559%2E582294%2EC87G0D)**
With a shocking number of families in New Hampshire having to ration gas and rely on food banks, some Republicans have quietly told Chris that they regret their vote in 2024 and they’re going to vote for him this November.
**I’m doing my part to help Chris earn enough votes to win this Senate seat. Will you join me?**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260827_2.-ZJF4k&amount=5&refcode=em20260827-2&t=22&akid=8559%2E582294%2EC87G0D)**
Did you know that the New Hampshire primary isn’t until September 8th?
The billionaires are already funding a storm of ads inaccurately portraying Chris as — well, as evil as _they_ are. Whatever you can afford to give will help Chris hold events in more places, reach more voters across party lines, and WIN on November 3rd.
**[With our help, Chris will be part of a 2027 Senate majority with a moral conscience.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260827_2.-ZJF4k&refcode=em20260827-2&t=23&akid=8559%2E582294%2EC87G0D)**
If you can’t afford to donate, here are two ways you can help for free.
**[Vote.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/695?t=24&akid=8559%2E582294%2EC87G0D)**
**[Volunteer.](https://act.chrispappas.org/signup/take_action_pappas_campaign/?source=em20260827-2&t=25&akid=8559%2E582294%2EC87G0D)**
Thank you, for reading this email and participating in whatever ways you can.
You’re stronger than you know, and we will get through this.
My best to you and your family,
\- Carole
Carole King is a singer-songwriter, author, and activist. Her distinctions include a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award, a Kennedy Center Honor, and double-induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. Now Carole is using her platform to help elect candidates who are running to lift and improve the lives of their fellow Americans. And she really did write this email.

Now I’m 58 years old, _and she is still my senator._
After 30 years in Washington, she’s become another corporate politician who does the bidding of her billionaire donors and Donald Trump. **_She’s voted with him 96% of the time._**
Mainers are sick and tired of her broken promises. But being in the Senate for half of my entire life means every single voter is gonna know who she is when they see her name on the ballot this November.
On the other hand, I’m a logger from Allagash who started this campaign just a couple of weeks ago.
Mainers know they don’t like Susan Collins. But they still need to learn more about me and how I will fight for the working families of Maine in the Senate.
My team and I are criss-crossing this state to talk to as many folks as we can, but the fastest way to reach every Mainer between now and November is our ads.
Peter, we need these ads running on TVs across Maine if we want any shot at winning on Election Day.

| Friends, We are 12 days away from the New Hampshire Democratic primary on September 8. We have 12 days to make sure voters across New Hampshire’s Second Congressional District know about Paige. Please keep sharing our campaign. [Share Our Message](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/pMNIfT5E2bLizQPrFX7CizlnYsATkLQ7/click?signature=43b169213dc1de9f939a54fa8b8bc3c35b020d12&url=https%3A%2F%2Flinktr.ee%2FPaigeForNH) **Our campaign is now using the Empower App**. Empower makes it easy to talk with people you already know about Paige and keep track of those conversations! You can [sign up here](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/pMNIfT5E2bLizQPrFX7CizlnYsATkLQ7/click?signature=022c64b43a48962e49b16d43a210bf0daaf58312&url=https%3A%2F%2Fweb2.getempower.com%2Fsignup%2Fpaige-ro). * * *
**What else can you do to Get Out the Vote? 🗳** If you live in New Hampshire and are not yet registered to vote, [here is what you need to know](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/pMNIfT5E2bLizQPrFX7CizlnYsATkLQ7/click?signature=a632bd95ad98e5dc70a28d7cf00f4bb0a7bdccb4&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sos.nh.gov%2Felections%2Fregister-vote). Review the [Election Day voting requirements](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/pMNIfT5E2bLizQPrFX7CizlnYsATkLQ7/click?signature=05f1e02adefcd04b3569514f456d618e25a52c82&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sos.nh.gov%2Felection-day-voting) to make sure you know what to bring. _Please note: Student IDs are no longer accepted as voter identification in New Hampshire._ Confirm [your polling station location and hours](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/pMNIfT5E2bLizQPrFX7CizlnYsATkLQ7/click?signature=0e0a6a2154e5d357cf109fad48b1245ca9968cb4&url=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.sos.nh.gov%2Fpollingplacesampleballot). Make sure you leave time in your day to get to vote. Consider anything else you need like childcare - kids are always welcome at the polls but depending upon your family's needs you may want another trusted adult to watch them while you vote. **Consider your friends, family and community 🏠** Do the people in your life have the information they need to vote? Share these resources with anyone who might need them. If someone you know needs a ride to the polls and you feel comfortable driving them, offer them a lift. **Most importantly** , [take care of yourself](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/pMNIfT5E2bLizQPrFX7CizlnYsATkLQ7/click?signature=394f0cb7d612eb1ccc3796b8fd6f1ab07b751456&url=https%3A%2F%2Fmakinithappen.org%2Felection-day-self-care-tips-for-all-of-us%2F) ✨ Questions, concerns, or feedback? Nixon is now set to face Senator Ashley Moody in November, a race that will decide whether a self-described democratic socialist represents President Trump's home state in the United States Senate.

Think about that. The first DSA candidate to win a Senate primary in 2026. In Florida. The state that has rejected every Democrat Senate candidate since 2012. The state with hundreds of thousands of Cuban and Venezuelan voters who fled socialism firsthand.

They chose a socialist anyway. And they are coming for this seat.

This is the latest in a growing string of socialist-aligned candidate victories in Democrat-on-Democrat contests across the country. New York. Michigan. Now Florida. _[**The domino effect is real and it is moving fast.**](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=e33d87e1574440bd8e11ca6567b18ee3&_e=s8_pU4wmHK7vi5C6bq3ugHNY0SXu4VsfrcHcYVxSKTUSASZcZf_Nc99hyedrTmYuH3itHdDV5htD5rvsKuKmTot-oU7QxnR6WBgwE6rL72T8VN1vGdvBo10T6my3vfdz3dBDvNSyKMPZg7o6wxhBkpKDtYgbWfPTXYeTd60Zip_8JM6Rx0lkNyndQ_a71xhr6R0e6F4tFOdHSmet-pEEAuaWef58TgebtNIA2o6zDVEB6WrFRUbFuuCrAMq8-BGp6y1yHl1zrOY7XBNIor0zvcw7wY0Lq-FDOB6pTolbTwuf6H4TiN8XNdLGTH5wBtbCoqgdNvufWbXAmYjAtv6ujM0k2MApirmb5cERfKEAxRNhgKBHUMN_c2MHMpYgn-gRwYjFLdw11LHI2efBXG1jzBz1-Z61KA5YU9-s7Uu_fLUNalV-5GsZlmeQ6-T-ZGyDFG7xDQ4arxlHvz6HXRLp5jlEMqEYbCWsxdDA2ma2rfFTemCvEP6o1jjtqEpWVvMPvYcPPjRD80I0NidTRVXpfX4eH3pH5HlyBaW8vitValzta2dfVEYiqVpbwHaNpCbZNnddWCMMECQImrohuufWQd1tGuRP4N0e3HgkrBI4kzFOUDyQSzRB669qmG98heJcXgKXHXhoLL4-qx4ldKxECtXpNK6RlTsefkLLagBb07F_Hw5vZh7HEWXpODmnP5YxcnXyWtp7hvKU7Vl1WtGydCCbpD_N8_RNTnGt-5-gkm40EydvKaggV_65Hb2eqCjp)_

Think about that. The first DSA candidate to win a Senate primary in 2026. In Florida. The state that has rejected every Democrat Senate candidate since 2012. | | For 91 years, Social Security has been an intergenerational promise for millions of people in Oregon and around the country. Today, about a million Oregonians depend on Social Security, and for a lot of them, it's virtually their entire income. Right now, that promise is in jeopardy, and Republicans refuse to act. Trump's layoffs of 7,500 Social Security workers have meant longer wait times and fewer people to help solve problems if something goes wrong with your benefits. More importantly, Social Security's trust fund is quickly running out of money. If we don't act, the trust fund that pays Social Security benefits runs dry in six years, and benefits could drop by more than 20% — for every single person who worked their whole life and paid into this system. And my Republican colleagues refuse to even bring a bill to the floor that would secure Social Security's solvency for the next 70 years. That's unacceptable. We need to fix this now, not when it's too late. You paid in, and you should be able to count on those benefits. I'm recommitting to fighting for a Social Security system that's fully funded, fully staffed, and here for the next 91 years too. Here's a
number that should stop you cold: 750.

That's how many times the Trump administration has been sued since taking
office.

And in more than 450 of those cases, judges have let Trump’s policies stay
in effect while the lawsuits are still being fought.

That's exactly Trump's plan. He's spent years installing judges who'll
shield his abuses of power, packing benches from federal district courts
up to the Supreme Court with loyalists who slow-walk justice while he does
the damage.

Look at where that's gotten us. Attacks on birthright citizenship. Frozen
funding to entire states. A Federal Reserve governor targeted over charges
that don't exist. A law firm punished for refusing his agenda. An
18th-century wartime law used to deport people with no due process.

Trump’s formula is simple: break the law, get sued, lean on the crony
judges he installed to keep the policy alive anyway. By the time a case is
finally decided, the harm's already done.

Demand Justice PAC exists to break that cycle, to expose how Trump
captured the courts and fight for a judiciary that answers to the
Constitution and the people, not to him.

We’ve met the critters that call the redwoods home, gone on our own berry foraging journey, and explored the strange and beautiful sights of the forest. This final round of Wood You Know? takes you up to the canopy, where we can see the redwood range in a whole new way: the scale, the texture, and the sheer expanse of green that makes these forests unlike anywhere else on Earth. It felt right to end this journey right back where we started—with the redwoods themselves. After all, every tiny detail we’ve explored this month exists because these giants are still standing. Most of all, thank you for being part of the reason these forests are still here to explore, in all their glory. See you out there! **Dan Meuser just said that before he accepts an invitation to debate me,**

| I have 267 sources into this piece. It is a 3 part series. Opinion: The great dividend diversion and its impact on Alaskan households By Phil Izon In “Opinion: Oil & gas history every Alaskan should know,” we followed Harold Heinze from the North Slope discovery wells to the creation of the Permanent Fund. His generation treated Alaska’s oil as a depletable asset that had to be converted into permanent wealth for future residents. That philosophy became the Fund itself. The 1982 statutory formula that created the Dividend made every Alaskan a shareholder. It was ownership, not a government program. That ownership has been dismantled. The Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend was never a discretionary government program. Rooted in the 1976 constitutional amendment and the 1982 statutory formula, it was a universal ownership right—every Alaskan a shareholder in the state’s resource wealth. The formula delivered transparent, predictable income insulated from annual politics. Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed. **I couldn't forget it.** **I couldn't stay silent.** I kept asking myself one question: **"What if it were my child?"** That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame.**
**Not for awards.**
**But because I believed people needed to see the truth.** For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.** And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Our mission is simple: **To stop the sale of God's children.**

| | | AIPAC-linked groups and their billionaire donors spent millions to keep Aisha Wahab out of Congress, Peter. **Now, they can call her Congresswoman-elect:** **[](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9hEtGUS8HMqdlPj3mh7ec2Bv5DLTWZK_Xawndo0vNWCt0yTwH0KWFYi67bUDmXmgUOlDtNzmw5i2gi31sI9ropm-FTwibJVPN1wK2oMHHOTFeCOXaxQAgME3EakxaprvRAQiBOXjbGXU9Ptjr4VkKA_ydMVPh4axbyYv-SKrzZmVqkr_kmt2201CEvX2dwuEQ5KtFZOH1zFCtqgEeGLuFMrnS7g8oyk3YDnB8ecP0TRs6z1Dw5za1W4PftZYAYVw0xfm7rvEMS80qXJeFLpIyScE7rJmNkmBzU0c4fiYhDylZfp3qJYOWATz-QfI1_-hJ2RvzPlOMAwVsXT2ns_x8aCqXhnaLR0d138ZUBxVs9Duqey71qzM5Wy-mJ_2V4kPbjjTliYMdZ-W_4g2vsvFmEw/4tj/UVMd1Fp5REOro10c4OSP9w/h0/h001.BgWlVOKHGr88X22k1RMjAv02EehA8tS96zAnRr6aKEc)** Last week, WFP-backed State Senator Aisha Wahab won the special election for California’s 14th Congressional District — **making history as the first Afghan-American elected to Congress.** AIPAC-linked groups went after Aisha because she's called for cutting off lethal military aid to Israel and has recognized the genocide in Gaza. So they threw millions of dollars and a barrage of attack ads into the race to stop her. **It didn’t work.** Aisha won, and she’ll now serve out the remainder of the current term through January 2027. But because this was a special election, the next race is already here. In November, Aisha will be back on the ballot — this time for a full two-year term in Congress. **[Split a contribution between Aisha’s campaign and the Working Families Party to help her win again this November and help us keep electing WFP champions at every level of government.](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9hEtGUS8HMqdlPj3mh7ec2Bv5DLTWZK_Xawndo0vNWCt0yTwH0KWFYi67bUDmXmgUYJiRfewmJaQQMpnNprpy24iDwIHpZtf9xiXu9ThfF22ovMQx9bY0FMKrdrUrDftVVQF4osZ__s3JU_lwJ6CYDmIQ8hjI-u462swzL215glEQYBBhTA25ZkuOS8S1If-1zEqC6vTgeHaQeo4RFUIYnB-Y4OGkqWAwsNrWpoPzLxXNMBxb-6t8rX_i1DoZ5vZ7RMhHTwHWfkfmJkhFZ2PP30vKYexVlmyEW9eOfqBVs5-nxS6ocLvWfq5TqnxlaFnifSSR-RvRnL4awgba0ejkB5pPFcCr1_4crfKw9ETWYtQov0om7JdwVwPlWYsfCNIMHstxbxfxp43wB4rxIfaPmg/4tj/UVMd1Fp5REOro10c4OSP9w/h1/h001.7JD2kAdZ1aLtHZH9IMLB45GjBwQ14f9iT6vfbDCqbBU)** **[Donate $10 »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9hEtGUS8HMqdlPj3mh7ec2Bv5DLTWZK_Xawndo0vNWCsLACJswAF4f1-Bl3U6yZRjQBsKURcONbWKCm5jKg5SU2FB9_P-hOiivXHFaaBHNnZrDibtABmKa5PPFrhGlih5cg29Lp-Hup6njlwdTbIxuAiYGayZbjGakbOTGPlGiayB0Hu02PEysBQwc5IAKHx4SrdxXKsW27HCxsqCoJiMyBoLrKI2tSMG4K2a7jA0bBbDith50wysvDmoKA7Tfksglhk6bpZJG4ozMIATUOZaO2x2whf2qmYTOcPJkhx3emBFonfYirQreeja8khU5IKgnaLcnhOOiFeRT1kcvoMmu4VH_NcLvT0Rc2pQ75y25wkSdMo3WBI8xYrq9OHUHwxs4ihEqpdiAHjjMya9y2sdCaCAF5yyL9Zo0qHHwI_7NvM/4tj/UVMd1Fp5REOro10c4OSP9w/h2/h001.ttIwpaROcJqfuIYIpikE265E9Ry0nfgYLfPwxg6bGeg)** **AIPAC and its billionaire donors have a pretty straightforward strategy, Peter: Spend whatever it takes to defeat candidates they don’t like — and make everyone else afraid to cross them.** The message is clear: Challenge their agenda, and they’ll make you their next multimillion-dollar target. **Well, Aisha got their message. She ran anyway — and she won.** And she’s not the only one. In Michigan, AIPAC-linked groups spent tens of millions trying to stop U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and other WFP champions — and came up short there, too. From Michigan to California, they’re learning an expensive lesson: **billionaire money can put its thumb on the scale, but it can’t always tip it.** Not when we have the resources to organize, reach voters, answer their attacks, and make sure people know exactly who is pouring millions into their elections — and why. That’s how we beat billionaire-backed groups from coast to coast.
