clean_body: | | | AIPAC-linked groups and their billionaire donors spent millions to keep Aisha Wahab out of Congress, Peter. Now, they can call her Congresswoman-elect: Last week, WFP-backed State Senator Aisha Wahab won the special election for California’s 14th Congressional District — making history as the first Afghan-American elected to Congress. AIPAC-linked groups went after Aisha because she's called for cutting off lethal military aid to Israel and has recognized the genocide in Gaza. So they threw millions of dollars and a barrage of attack ads into the race to stop her. It didn’t work. Aisha won, and she’ll now serve out the remainder of the current term through January 2027. But because this was a special election, the next race is already here. In November, Aisha will be back on the ballot — this time for a full two-year term in Congress. AIPAC and its billionaire donors have a pretty straightforward strategy, Peter: Spend whatever it takes to defeat candidates they don’t like — and make everyone else afraid to cross them. The message is clear: Challenge their agenda, and they’ll make you their next multimillion-dollar target. Well, Aisha got their message. She ran anyway — and she won. And she’s not the only one. In Michigan, AIPAC-linked groups spent tens of millions trying to stop U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and other WFP champions — and came up short there, too. From Michigan to California, they’re learning an expensive lesson: billionaire money can put its thumb on the scale, but it can’t always tip it. Not when we have the resources to organize, reach voters, answer their attacks, and make sure people know exactly who is pouring millions into their elections — and why. That’s how we beat billionaire-backed groups from coast to coast. And with Aisha back on the ballot this November, we need to be ready to do it again. In solidarity, always, Working Families Party P.S. AIPAC can keep hauling billionaire money from Michigan to California and from one race to the next. They can keep shopping around for an election they think they can buy. But we’re building something they can’t pack up and move: a movement rooted everywhere, ready to meet them wherever they go. Thanks for being in this fight with us. Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. Reply directly to this email and let us know. This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. If you received this email as a forward and want to get the latest updates from the Working Families Party directly, The Working Families Party is the party of the multiracial working class, fighting for a nation that cares for all of us. Wanna learn more? And if you need to update your contact information, Other political groups have corporate donors. But we can pool our resources too. | | | Washington votes by mail. **_98.5% of us._** The second-highest rate in America.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138057010/642821380/-995582223?refcode=260827-vbm&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZTUyYzk0NC01ZGEyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTliZWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ad7v-GiKIBllEa8pUXA80Pk1d92Wq4yXzEq234M2GoI=)
---
So when the Supreme Court greenlit Trump's executive order restricting mail ballots this week, that wasn't some D.C. legal story for us. That was the federal government reaching for the way an ENTIRE STATE votes. **Let me be blunt about what this order does:** it puts DC bureaucrats in charge of deciding whose ballots the Postal Service delivers. Unelected officials, 3,000 miles away, inserting themselves between you and your ballot box. I represent loggers, mechanics, farmers, and nurses — people who may not agree with each other on everything. **_But nobody in this district_****, right or left, wants the federal government touching their ballot. That's not a partisan feeling out here. That's a line.** And here's the thing about this district: we're the toss-up everyone says decides the House. They know it. That's exactly why making voting harder helps them — and exactly why I won't let it. [**Our answer isn't to panic. It's to step on the gas: that is why I am asking you to rush a $25 donation now to help us fight back and drive a turnout too big to rig. **](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138057011/642821381/-995582223?refcode=260827-vbm&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZTUyYzk0NC01ZGEyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTliZWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ad7v-GiKIBllEa8pUXA80Pk1d92Wq4yXzEq234M2GoI=)

subject: Glass half full

body:
I know it’s difficult to stay optimistic

I’ll be honest: I’ve always been a glass-half-full kind of person. In times like these, I know it can be difficult to stay optimistic — or even hopeful — about our country’s future. But I am. And I hope you are too. But Derek, I want to be clear: **That optimism doesn’t make me naive.** I know the stakes are high. I know nothing is set in stone. And I know that a far-right Governor could reverse all the progress we’ve made together. [_**So today, I’m asking you to stay hopeful and prepared. Please, can you chip in**_** _$10 _**_**right away to help us reach our End-of-Month fundraising goal, double down on our voter outreach programs, and keep the far-right out of power here in the most competitive state in the country?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138056990/642821302/-1944933843?refcode=email_082726_optimism&amounts=10,25,50,100,250,500,1000&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwMWViNDVlMi01Y2EyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTliZWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=sA0x_yZ-MJoQPKrZCYXjYlT5mNqXV4vZEVyBsoUGCTg=) | | [Donate →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138056991/642821303/-1944933843?refcode=email_082726_optimism&amounts=10,25,50,100,250,500,1000&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwMWViNDVlMi01Y2EyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTliZWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=sA0x_yZ-MJoQPKrZCYXjYlT5mNqXV4vZEVyBsoUGCTg=)

As we approach November, I’m feeling optimistic, Derek. But that doesn’t mean we can sit back and watch from the sidelines. The far-right has all the same information we have — and we know they won’t take their ball and go home.
We have to stay ready. We have to stay vigilant. We have to stay prepared. And Derek, we can only do that with your help.
Thank you,
Josh

Peter,
I need to speak with you directly.
**Democrats in Florida just nominated a self-proclaimed socialist in the biggest Senate special election of 2026.**
_**Her name is Angie Nixon. ** _
She publicly and proudly joined the Democratic Socialists of America during her campaign.
She’s a former “community organizer” who literally runs a bookstore called Cafe Resistance.
She’s endorsed by The Squad and held one of her final rallies with Hamas superfan Rashida Tlaib.
**And she just defeated an incredibly well-funded Democrat with a nearly $17 million war chest** _**by more than ten points after raising less than a million dollars.** _
This is not a fringe candidate who stumbled into a nomination. And the socialist movement gobbling up seats all across the country can no longer be excused as some obscure “wing” of the Democratic Party.
**The heart and soul and energy of the Democrats is now with the socialists, and with the support of President Trump and patriots all across the nation, I’m ready to bury this twisted ideology in Florida.**
You and I love this country. We love freedom, the rule of law, and the belief that hard work and responsibility matter. We do not get up every day and work hard, raise our families and build our communities just to see the evil and failed socialist ideology destroy everything we love.
_**This is the line in the sand.** _

After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages, I fought back. A whole bunch of politicians, including then-first-term Senator Susan Collins, promised to listen, but they left us high and dry — and I realized that nothing would change unless there were working-class voices in power.

So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life to fight for working people.

I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol, because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district that went for Trump by 20 points, because up here, people care less about a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family.

| | _With just twelve days until the primary, I am using each day to discuss an issue I have highlighted on the campaign trail. For Day 12, I am highlighting the need for federal and local government to work together to protect our communities from climate change._
* * *
Dear David, Some people encounter climate change as an abstraction: a graph, a headline, a wildfire somewhere else. But coastal communities like Hampton encounter it as surprise expenses, higher municipal budgets, and rising property taxes. It shows up in rising flood insurance premiums, in crumbling and quickly deteriorating roads and sidewalks, sewer systems inundated with salt water, and in homeowners who can’t sell because prospective buyers can't get mortgages after underwriters have seen the maps. **[Taking meaningful action on climate change will require pairing a local focus on the issue with bold, federal action. If you’re ready to help me head to Congress and fight for a Washington that supports local communities in this fight, please pitch in today:](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/_-sVpwU__nkZGYRYxHnAng~~/AAUS1hA~/uXJr-cUeDoxJ-lPFWM4uO18LMTk9v_yl3wbAcO9CTY0Mr-jzpAKWy-Df4Ch1CtYHPZSMlvbT2_5qv0hrCz8cnRKZ-0xdF2qbySgNuYE_9jxhlSlKy3pMS-HLQGk8IyeG-WWgWeQP_awOjxFW5MqgMXavfueWtrknPiqhCQofV7nXJ1XS8PRx515S0W3fqOTaJXgYvN0nK0Wx_EukAVikKrztevWfnXqUwHjtMZOgzm-o8tTgVSTvzelkWxE9h6Wy2pre1cNMkWA5Va0HrXnmaA~~)** | | [DONATE](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/_-sVpwU__nkZGYRYxHnAng~~/AAUS1hA~/uXJr-cUeDoxJ-lPFWM4uO18LMTk9v_yl3wbAcO9CTY0Mr-jzpAKWy-Df4Ch1CtYHPZSMlvbT2_5qv0hrCz8cnRKZ-0xdF2qbySgNuYE_9jxhlSlKy3pMS-HLQGk8IyeG-WWgWeQP_awOjxFW5MqgMXavfueWtrknPiqhCQofV7nXJ1XS8PRx515S0W3fqOTaJXgYvN0nK0Wx_EukAVikKrztevWfnXqUwHjtMZOgzm-o8tTgVSTvzelkWxE9h6Wy2pre1cNMkWA5Va0HrXnmaA~~)
---
Many politicians in Washington _want_ to help, David, but the way that help is structured means that small towns can barely access it.
Major federal resilience programs are built around the assumption that every applicant has a grants office, a capital reserve, and months to produce a benefit-cost analysis. **Most towns have one staff person wearing six hats, and my town, Hampton, only has _two_!**
The programs that work the best are also the ones on the chopping block. The NOAA coastal programs that made Hampton's Roadmap possible, like the Coastal Zone Management Act, the National Sea Grant program, and the state Coastal Program are among the smallest line items in the federal budget and among the first targeted when budget fights begin. Dollar for dollar, these are some of the most effective federal investments we make.
Crafting legislation that addresses the climate crisis in a Congress that is frequently mired in partisan gridlock requires a specific local focus with an emphasis on results. Here is what I will push for in Congress:
* **Funding the small programs that work,** like the NOAA's Office for Coastal Management, the Coastal Zone Management Act, Sea Grant, and the state Coastal Programs that distribute federal support to towns. These cost pennies on the dollar and buy real planning and action on the ground.
* **Rewriting federal resilience grants so small towns can access and use them.** Cut the match requirements that disqualify communities that need the help most, and simplify the application burden for towns under a population threshold.
* **Funding coastal resilience like infrastructure, not like a sweepstakes.** Move toward predictable, formula-based resilience funding that lets communities plan beyond a single grant cycle.
* **Reforming the National Flood Insurance Program** around honesty and affordability, modernizing flood maps, and protecting primary-residence affordability for working- and middle-class families already living in floodplains, while pricing new development in high-risk areas fairly. Taxpayers should not be repeatedly rebuilding luxury second homes.
* **Treating working waterfronts as the infrastructure they are.** Fisheries, ports, and small coastal businesses are not amenities; they are economies and communities. Federal policy needs to account for that.

**None of this “solves” climate change, but it mitigates the worst impacts while we get serious about addressing the root causes.** It's meant to keep small coastal communities afloat (and our property taxes steady).
**[We need a more robust federal response to the climate crisis, but we also need to make sure that our local communities have the resources they need to survive in the face of the most catastrophic impacts of climate change. I’m running for Congress to make sure we do both at the same time. Can you support this work by pitching in today?](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/_-sVpwU__nkZGYRYxHnAng~~/AAUS1hA~/uXJr-cUeDoxJ-lPFWM4uO18LMTk9v_yl3wbAcO9CTY0Mr-jzpAKWy-Df4Ch1CtYHPZSMlvbT2_5qv0hrCz8cnRKZ-0xdF2qbySgNuYE_9jxhlSlKy3pMS-HLQGk8IyeG-WWgWeQP_awOjxFW5MqgMXavfueWtrknPiqhCQofV7nXJ1XS8PRx515S0W3fqOTaJXgYvN0nK0Wx_EukAVikKrztevWfnXqUwHjtMZOgzm-o8tTgVSTvzelkWxE9h6Wy2pre1cNMkWA5Va0HrXnmaA~~)**

name: Major General Paul Eaton, U.S. Army, retired
subject: Clearing the way for the Arc de Trump
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY VOTEVETS, VOTEVETS
body:
A federal commission packed with Trump appointees voted 8 to 1 to advance the Arc de Trump
#
Peter, I need to tell you where the fight to stop Trump’s arch stands, because it’s getting worse.
A federal commission packed with Trump appointees voted 8 to 1 to advance the Arc de Trump — 250 feet tall, sitting on Memorial Circle, at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery.
They heard nearly three hours of public opposition first. Veterans. Families. People who understand what that place means to this country. The commission listened, then voted to advance the arch anyway.
This isn't final. But it's closer than it's ever been.
The sightline between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington was designed on purpose — a quiet symbol of a reunited country — and Trump wants to put a monument to himself in the middle of it.
I've spent enough of my life on the grounds of Arlington National Cemetery to know its gravity. My father, killed in action during the Vietnam War, is buried there. Men who I trained, who served under me are buried there. It is not the backdrop for some draft-dodging coward’s vanity.
So we're asking for $5. That's it.
$5 because Trump’s commission could force this through before most people even hear what’s happened.
$5 because we're up against a President who's made this one of the top priorities of his administration.
But really, $5 or anything you can afford. Because whatever you can give, right now, matters more than the amount itself.
[**Can we count on you? Chip in that $5 and help VoteVets raise enough hell that they can't force the Arc de Trump through in secret. Enough to stop this, once and for all.**](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-aug26.uvTq9l&refcode=em260827-1-360&t=1&akid=35511%2E3013755%2E5bZbVP)

clean_body: A federal commission packed with Trump appointees voted 8 to 1 to advance the Arc de Trump Peter, I need to tell you where the fight to stop Trump’s arch stands, because it’s getting worse. A federal commission packed with Trump appointees voted 8 to 1 to advance the Arc de Trump — 250 feet tall, sitting on Memorial Circle, at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery. They heard nearly three hours of public opposition first. Veterans. Families. People who understand what that place means to this country. The commission listened, then voted to advance the arch anyway. This isn't final. But it's closer than it's ever been. The sightline between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington was designed on purpose — a quiet symbol of a reunited country — and Trump wants to put a monument to himself in the middle of it. I've spent enough of my life on the grounds of Arlington National Cemetery to know its gravity. My father, killed in action during the Vietnam War, is buried there. Men who I trained, who served under me are buried there. It is not the backdrop for some draft-dodging coward’s vanity. So we're asking for $5. That's it. $5 because Trump’s commission could force this through before most people even hear what’s happened. $5 because we're up against a President who's made this one of the top priorities of his administration. Peter,

In a moment, we're going to ask you to chip in $10 to fund a ballot chasing operation in Arizona. Please give us a chance to explain why, right now, this matters more than almost anything else we're doing.

Here is the truth:

Horrible Katie Hobbs is standing directly in the way of an America First White House in **2028**. She knows it. The radical left knows it. And they know the road there runs straight through Arizona.

**The Red Wall starts in 2026.**

Democrats know this too. That is why they are pouring **BILLIONS of dollars** into Arizona right now - buying ads, hiring consultants, and flooding this state with cash to make sure Katie Hobbs and the radical left keep their grip on it.

We don't have billions. We have something they can't buy: **you.**

Let me explain why Arizona matters so much right now.

**ONE:** Arizona is contested ground. It's one of the states that will decide who controls the road to the White House in 2028. Whoever wins here now sets the terms for what comes next.

**TWO:** Arizona is growing fast. More people, more Congressional seats, more say in who runs this country. Whoever builds real relationships with these voters today owns the future of this state.

**THREE:** Registered Republicans outnumber registered Democrats in Arizona. We already have the voters. What we don't have yet is enough people on the ground to reach every single one of them before Election Day.

Here's how we close that gap:

Turning Point PAC funds ballot chasers - our ballot chasing program that sends trained teams into Arizona communities months before Election Day to build real relationships with voters, not just knock on doors the weekend before the polls open.

That is exactly why we're working to fund the training of **100 NEW ballot chasers in Arizona right now.**

But we need to fund this training. Right now.

Every ballot chaser we fund has to be trained, equipped, and put in the field. Every $10 you chip in goes directly toward getting one more of these 100 ballot chasers ready to go.

Peter, I won't pretend we can match Horrible Katie Hobbs and the Democrats dollar for dollar. Nobody can outspend billions.

body:
Wake Up. Equip. Mobilize.
| | | August 27, 2026 | [**Read Online**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/lmu2rmld6efmhndq4w0f6h8d46mzxsgh4dogv/qvh8h7hdk884l7blhk/aHR0cHM6Ly9ja2FyY2hpdmUuY29tL2IvcWR1OGg3aDRsZXZxN3R6d25ubXc3dThucnd4cXZ0NGhrb3Z4OQ==) |
---

Friends,
Today we’re doing something we’ve never done before.
We’re building something new — and we’re asking you to help build it with us.
But first, let me name something we all already feel: the distance between the American people and Washington, D.C. It’s real, it’s grown for decades, and no speech from either party has closed it. We all know the truth in our bones — government will not fix itself. It never has. Renewal in this country has only ever come from one place: the people.
And when the American people decide to build something together, it gets built. A collection of farmers and shopkeepers stood up to the most powerful empire on earth — and won. A generation of ordinary Americans retooled their factories in a matter of months and became the arsenal that saved the free world. And when we decided to put a man on the moon, we did it in less than a decade — with slide rules and shirt sleeves.
That’s why we know we can do this too. Together, we can do anything.
**WAKE UP** : Last week a reporter wrote asking about _Trapped: Detroit_. Because Catherine didn’t give them the conspiracy clickbait they were looking for, the article never ran — but her comments were so on point I wanted to share part of them with you:
_“Trapped: Detroit is not a film about an election. It is years of struggle in Detroit’s inner city, condensed into thirty-three minutes of interviews with people who checked their own voter records and found ballots already cast in their names. A mother of six who has never voted in her life, carried on the rolls in 2020 as an absentee voter. A transit worker who voted in person, but was canceled out by a mailed ballot he never requested. A 53-year-old man who has never cast a ballot, but is a recent and regular voter on paper. Nine of them filed suit in federal court. They were told they lacked standing to complain about their own names._

_Nobody asked those people how they vote. It wasn’t relevant, and it still isn’t. What was taken from them sits underneath politics entirely — the right to a voice that counts, and is counted. Those nine people didn’t wake up because someone gave a speech. They woke up because they looked at their own records. That’s what waking up actually means here — not being persuaded, but checking.”_
**EQUIP** : Catherine shared something else in that letter that matters even more for what comes next:
_“We’ve spent fifteen years raising awareness, and now people are aware, but that was never our ultimate goal. Our goal was to help correct the brokenness in our electoral process: the plumbing, the paperwork, the unglamorous software and machinery that decides whether an election can be trusted.”_
Awareness was never the finish line. So we built the tools — the platforms, the data, the capability to check a roll and document what’s there. All of it is now open to any aligned, engaged citizen who wants to use it. You don’t need our permission and you don’t need to be an expert. You need the tools and someone to show you how they work.
That’s what your membership funds first: putting those tools in the hands of everyone who asks.
**MOBILIZE** : One person with a public records request is easy to dismiss — but 10,000 requests across eight thousand county offices is not.
That’s the strategy.
Not one organization litigating alone — a distributed movement of citizens doing lawful, documented, unglamorous work in their own counties, at the same time, on the record.
It cannot be intimidated out of existence, because there is no single place to apply the pressure.
And it means that when [_Trapped: Detroit_](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/lmu2rmld6efmhndq4w0f6h8d46mzxsgh4dogv/g3hnh5hmqeel0lurh9/aHR0cHM6Ly90cmFwcGVkLnZvdGU=) is released and the attacks start rolling in — and they are coming — we absorb them, because the funding isn’t from three large donors who can be pressured. It’s a million Americans who decided this was their cause.
So today we are launching [**Mobilize A Million**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/lmu2rmld6efmhndq4w0f6h8d46mzxsgh4dogv/9qhzhnhd5gg6exu9h3/aHR0cHM6Ly9tb2JpbGl6ZWFtaWxsaW9uLmNhdGhlcmluZS1kMzkud29ya2Vycy5kZXYv).
[](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/lmu2rmld6efmhndq4w0f6h8d46mzxsgh4dogv/3ohphkh3pqq2k9trhn/aHR0cHM6Ly9tb2JpbGl6ZWFtaWxsaW9uLmNhdGhlcmluZS1kMzkud29ya2Vycy5kZXY=)
---
Not another fundraiser. This is a campaign to put one million Americans into the ranks of this work — awake to what’s broken, equipped to check it themselves, and organized well enough that the people who benefit from the brokenness can no longer count on our silence.
Here’s what your membership builds:
**WAKE UP** : Grow our network of state-level alliances that build communities and pave the way for oversight and transparency at the local level.
**EQUIP** : Fund poll observer training through our Volunteer Programs, sustain legal defense against the coordinated lawfare and media attacks we absorb, and put True the Vote’s citizen engagement tools into more hands:
* **IV3** — voter record confirmation and efficient, ineligible-voter challenges to clean bloated voter rolls
* **Scan.Check.Protect.** — check your voter registration on the go
* **VoteAlert** — real-time reporting of election fraud and election procedure failures

**MOBILIZE** : Step into the ranks yourself — and bring your neighbors with you. Share this message with everyone in your network.
Whether it’s a dollar a month or a thousand, we need you. Every. Dollar. Matters.
But more than the dollar — we need you in the ranks.
**Join Mobilize A Million today** : https://mobilizeamillion.catherine-d39.workers.dev/
Our Republic will not survive to the next generation unless we unite citizens for real change: free and fair elections — today and ever onward.
We’ve never done this before. We’re building something new. Build it with us.
Wake up. Equip. Mobilize.
It’s time. Join us. We will walk this journey together.
For Freedom,
Sarah

Friend, Tomorrow is National Black Giving Day to support Black-led organizations, which are often underfunded and get only 1-2% of philanthropic funding. **I’m proud to work alongside****[Detroit Justice Center](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvx7QQDKFwkQMBaEt-a9W1TnMXNfnqoiklv_TSLlYzO0P5opz-Y0MbaH0wmODV_tSZuNLnSXYczo0JyMvQu5hGCrwbOAOiQ92a6dnXl1VO3hZ9GRFnrcO3KwbWNseToKYSPXsR_AckZjngdQ2T2RtVHPL6Qe0d6ucK4iWjeCH8bdNHvIsBButhUEyJtU7aEm1Q09MX36X4XVmstEv1DCWlKf3-WcA_JyNI7NDLHhZG3p5_Bi8IV7z9GMijD_3uaIElG4Wo7WxLS1G9MXFe35W4XddMGblp929UEUuj09pOfeMbwKmmMJZS4IBNvJvvIqGXTLl9yzn4B_-SNZtM81uHsWtzROVUZw9IfPDIvZR_M7HRz9cy_HRBmV9usefWsf8oqIbOuZXkxy4Q1MHuhqs4e/4tj/LpoCuxqaQeeLzr52HT_FwA/h1/h001.Enb5V1D55cHnX7jWWgMN-HjRaCRGVCWyO8-L3PZCCxw)****, a Black-led non-profit law firm that’s a national leader in the fight to transform the criminal legal system and build equitable cities where everyone thrives.** The group has won transformative victories to protect our right to protest, clear criminal records, and end profit-seeking predatory policing. While fighting for systemic change, Detroit Justice Center also provides free legal services to keep clients out of jail, out of poverty, and in their homes. This includes helping pay off people’s court debt, restoring drivers’ licenses, clearing warrants for unpaid fees, assisting in eviction cases, defending against unjust landlords, dismissing charges against protestors, and helping people keep their water on. As a thought partner, Detroit Justice Center uplifts the needs of currently and formerly incarcerated people — helping shape my policies to:
* advance housing justice, including removing barriers to housing for people with criminal records, who are 13x more likely to be unhoused
* push back against the unjust cash bail system and the debt-to-jail pipeline that keeps people locked in cycles of poverty
* shift public funds to community needs rather than state violence
* ensure access to body camera footage without financial barriers

As a former movement lawyer, I’m inspired by Detroit Justice Center’s lawyers who represent protesters, such as anti-war students and people impacted by police brutality — and successfully get their charges dismissed.
The group also provides legal support to formerly incarcerated people who are seeking to start businesses, as well as tenants’ unions and people who are pursuing economic models that put people over profit.
Detroit Justice Center has established 6 community land trusts for permanently affordable housing and 12 worker-owned cooperatives led by Black women and women of color, including a childcare collective, green grocer, and mobile wellness hub.
The group has helped thousands of Michiganders clear the hurdle of suspended licenses, which can spiral into lost jobs and mounting court debt. And now they’re spreading this program to other states.
They’re also collaborating with groups across the country to expand community-led approaches to harm that prioritize healing and accountability over punishment.

Hey folks,
Trump's White House is miserable, Republicans are staring down a brutal political environment, and Democrats have a real opportunity in front of us. But only if we stop letting the right decide what we're supposed to be talking about.
[Jack Cocchiarella](https://open.substack.com/users/112946688-jack-cocchiarella?utm_source=mentions) and I talked Trump, MAGA's terrible candidates, independent media, Hasan Piker, AIPAC, the DSA, and what Democrats actually need to do to win.
Here are a few moments you don't want to miss:
* [**00:02:24**] I preview the debates I'm headed into in Las Vegas--from Trump's corruption to free speech, political violence, and constitutional rights.
* [**00:08:04**] We dig into Trump's collapsing political position, his terrible numbers, and why people fleeing his White House should still expect accountability.
* [**00:13:18**] We get into the absolutely disastrous candidates Republicans are putting forward--and why Trump's grip on the GOP could cost them races they have no business losing.
* [**00:19:39**] Jack and I have a real disagreement about Hasan Piker, antisemitism, Israel, AIPAC, and the responsibility that comes with having a massive political platform.
* [**00:25:05**] We bring it back to the bigger picture: Trump remains the center of the political universe, and Democrats cannot waste this moment by fighting on terrain Republicans choose for us.

This conversation gets funny, uncomfortable, serious, and occasionally a little messy--which is exactly why I think it's worth watching. We talk about the political opportunity Democrats have right now, but also the independent media ecosystem we need to build if we actually want to shape the conversation instead of constantly reacting to the right.
**That independence matters. We can chase stories corporate media ignores. We can disagree without turning every disagreement into a civil war. And we can keep the focus where it belongs: defeating MAGA, holding corruption accountable, and building something better.**
**If you value honest conversations like this, help us keep them going.**

name: Roy Cooper
subject: It’s going to be close
body:
Peter,
We got word about a brand-new poll here in North Carolina, and it’s not looking good:
Following the millions of dollars the GOP has been pouring into attack ads against me, **a brand-new poll out last week shows Michael Whatley and I are statistically tied.** If that’s all you need to hear today, please use this link to split a donation between our campaign and Wes Moore and stop them from taking the lead: **[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20260827-2?refcode=em-20260827-2](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260827-2.NU5hFt&refcode=em-20260827-2&t=1&akid=1831%2E1086043%2EpmKi_p)**
North Carolina hasn’t sent a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 2008 -- and Republicans want it to stay that way. They know that if we fail to flip this seat, we’ll lose our chance at taking back the U.S. Senate majority.
This new poll only confirms what we’ve known all along: this is going to be an extremely close race. And I’m going to need all the help I can get.
I’ve been a top target for national Republicans all cycle. So far, GOP super PACs are pouring nearly $100 million into this race so far to try and defeat me.
I’ve spent much of my life fighting for North Carolinians, but alone I can’t out-organize all the GOP’s dark money. Unlike Whatley, who relies on special interests and dark money to win, our campaign depends on grassroots supporters like you.
**[Will you chip in $5 between our campaign and Wes Moore to help me fight back and win?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260827-2.NU5hFt&refcode=em-20260827-2&t=2&akid=1831%2E1086043%2EpmKi_p)**

Thank you,
Roy Cooper

subject: "Magnificent"

body:
| It’s an attack on press freedom unlike any in modern memory.
---
[](https://eboq88hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001RKhyWobkFxmjAfgeqr2O2exeGmecLMfvRPeTdKkKNxgOJY5YnlJkAhEPQH75VtqoGv2ZbjVihf6kEho4GBLRLm3CFEjZA7LzltAeh0LwKd7MUwHBEPS0kgw7Bjq7evy6ZMdqsQyEQlLuALMXK30Yal4GhK5vie9_A5YhnFjdMxxdSez-kXKcAWpzgAwuYUpup0KYxe7UA-Zb0kUFVhTiytxIL4-T8My8Dq6Dqq5x7fgkAdmUPdOsIUfqH6wcCMmuBKNSqy0_6Uqnt51Li5d0og==&c=M-XgC1-4dDwQvEKWSYwjfI2rZjEIy-849sjPCkaElbYhE9q--uYBKQ==&ch=f4e8F7ajb4XSkVFgDnuShYWDyqRFWrgz5jLyonmfv-W3Nm3r8HoPdg==)
By now, folks, you’ve probably heard the story. Qatar gifts our president a 250-foot, $400 million luxury jet. The president wants it to replace Air Force One. Fast-tracks some upgrades. Calls it “magnificent,” and boasts about it. **It turns out — according to _The New York Times_ — that the aircraft is lacking essential national security components, and is reportedly missing missile defense systems and the wiring to shield against an electromagnetic pulse attack.** So the Justice Department subpoenaed the phone records of the four journalists who broke that story, went after their relatives’ phone records too, and backed down only last week when a federal judge pushed back. It was one of the most blatant attacks on the free press in American history, and it will not be the last. It’s also why I immediately opened up an investigation into these abuses. **I will not let Donald Trump and his acolytes intimidate reporters into silence without exposing, at every turn, exactly what they are trying to hide from the American people.** But I can’t do it alone, especially when Republicans hold the majority in the Senate and use it to shield the president. **[Will you pitch in any amount, even $10, to help us uplift the Democrats running in this November’s elections?](https://eboq88hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001RKhyWobkFxmjAfgeqr2O2exeGmecLMfvRPeTdKkKNxgOJY5YnlJkAhEPQH75VtqoGv2ZbjVihf6kEho4GBLRLm3CFEjZA7LzltAeh0LwKd7MUwHBEPS0kgw7Bjq7evy6ZMdqsQyEQlLuALMXK30Yal4GhK5vie9_A5YhnFjdMxxdSez-kXKcAWpzgAwuYUpup0KYxe7UA-Zb0kUFVhTiytxIL4-T8My8Dq6Dqq5x7fgkAdmUPdOsIUfqH6wcCMmu8D5XYoJ9aMAuuo39bJeKZQ==&c=M-XgC1-4dDwQvEKWSYwjfI2rZjEIy-849sjPCkaElbYhE9q--uYBKQ==&ch=f4e8F7ajb4XSkVFgDnuShYWDyqRFWrgz5jLyonmfv-W3Nm3r8HoPdg==)** _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | [DONATE $10→](https://eboq88hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001RKhyWobkFxmjAfgeqr2O2exeGmecLMfvRPeTdKkKNxgOJY5YnlJkAhEPQH75VtqoGv2ZbjVihf6kEho4GBLRLm3CFEjZA7LzltAeh0LwKd7MUwHBEPS0kgw7Bjq7evy6ZMdqsQyEQlLuALMXK30Yal4GhK5vie9_A5YhnFjdMxxdSez-kXKcAWpzgAwuYUpup0KYxe7UA-Zb0kUFVhTiytxIL4-T8My8Dq6Dqq5x7fgkAdmUPdOsIUfqH6wcCMmuh1vP8zG7bIcZ6IEL0BWhmQ==&c=M-XgC1-4dDwQvEKWSYwjfI2rZjEIy-849sjPCkaElbYhE9q--uYBKQ==&ch=f4e8F7ajb4XSkVFgDnuShYWDyqRFWrgz5jLyonmfv-W3Nm3r8HoPdg==)

Peter, As the midterms approach, millions of us are watching the headlines and wondering, _will my voice be heard this year?_ From the SAVE Act to attacks on mail-in ballots and the Voting Rights Act, our right to vote is under assault. **And the Supreme Court, an institution we’ve looked to for decades to protect our rights, is in on it.** Bought by dark money, the Court is no longer working for the people. Instead, it has morphed into a key player in the Trump administration’s attempt to systematically dismantle our voting rights. When voting rights are weakened, our power to create change takes a blow. We cannot let that happen. [**That’s why this TOMORROW, August 28, we are fighting to protect our rights at the March on Washington: Defend the Vote. Can you join us?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.A3cd-kVlFz1CzUMSYeTvVTlJ9brtK9B32JPJ_JT5Q5PonQB1pJAEsjjWsDPHaE5G79cFTTm9BLfekhGY-m0A4SOjst18tVEE0cNRCmU-vzctESlXyaEVCzv9sRwb9gix5KflsCmM7t1AvYI7zJeJntWrGWjQne9Jstsz4oMsGiKV5_X0WjuvtXO0Q7LBr99b_vo-hnxLKmluz3sDHyELqh1xaedZ69QRNtMm0RqhOTSwzoKq220A67X-dVvSGvB-5S_HZ4fqMOqItIv4obkTxDm_pL155l_9foupAfSMrsw/4tj/J1KKuRqjQpaz2vA7FzM2Lg/h0/h001.1hqAVDz-sV5gKbc3y48p-17A86N4GtPMhjcl26UJFb4) The date is no accident. It marks the 63rd anniversary of the 1963 March on Washington, where Martin Luther King Jr. gave his _I Have A Dream_ speech. **That March built the momentum that led to the Voting Rights Act of 1965.** **The Voting Rights Act, created to end racial discrimination in voting, has been called “the single most effective” piece of legislation created by our government.** 1 For decades, Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act allowed (and at times required) states to create majority-minority districts so that minority communities could elect candidates of their choice and have a voice in our government. The Supreme Court’s _Callais_ decision gutted that provision, declaring Louisiana’s district maps “an unconstitutional racial gerrymander.” And since _Callais_ , multiple states are scrambling to redraw their districts _without majority-minority districts_ before the midterms.2 **A dark money fueled Court may be trying to silence our voices at the polls, but we the people still have the power.** That’s why we are inviting you to join us in making history again for the March on Washington: Defend the Vote. **The right to vote belongs to all of us.** That’s why this march, convened by the National Action Network and the Drum Major Institute and co-chaired by Rev. Al Sharpton, Martin Luther King III, and Andrea Waters King, _is nonpartisan, interfaith, intergenerational, and open to people from every community._ [**Sixty-three years ago, we made history and lit the spark that created the Voting Rights Act. Tomorrow, we will make history defending our right to vote again. Join us and RSVP here.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.A3cd-kVlFz1CzUMSYeTvVTlJ9brtK9B32JPJ_JT5Q5PonQB1pJAEsjjWsDPHaE5G79cFTTm9BLfekhGY-m0A4dbnE0Y1voYWRH8lddHcRfKK3sdq8nAVYd0Yi1OizYjR4nqiBreeKhRttTMct68u9m7-65RVoJbfBLX_cVakFyFHsdc5lZ46znny0Z_f8YXdLaJ013n_Xacy2c0-ztKHzll6XEL1uVgBAdrrwK5lbyvZXpjJDTzcgf-pbIudKTCntsAfIejwzoLu-8cj-FIHaBYWxl9dONt5How65ouw19s/4tj/J1KKuRqjQpaz2vA7FzM2Lg/h1/h001.pQ4jRe1-FhSDJdSrUuW_IrOZ_WBO1qbahWbD1L4HC3M) In Solidarity, United for Democracy 1 [https://www.justice.gov/crt/introduction-federal-voting-rights-laws-0](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMUMcdv958xYsa3V1c0O4pz2sumVESy2T-9IaNYgar5pkSYCOXGLxmWWZw8KtrGEgJ_JWnznfW4IJmBoXUp8Dm-VWmUk4ogzRHL7oN38ytuUk5FzcU3LurS6RrTjSItzSJAb6X3Ln4bUAttbHo0nDSaaIF99kmp9FzsYhKlQUtGkSBCfNwHMyoR-tvhtb2INdRFKnDqorPw-a1GngbeE_kz4e9IdFdiOHwT6Jo8a-giS5CqSjyTvwu2MtTiIGteng_Yw5wWwCnHiGEoWZ2lSZCx4/4tj/J1KKuRqjQpaz2vA7FzM2Lg/h2/h001.vP4elbyDyvZjZEPmul6cwEvSBda2pcPd2cOrnoK9iCs)

body:
Nation’s largest grassroots pro-life organization backs Letlow in Louisiana Senate race

| | |

| | | | | | FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASEAugust 27, 2026[katherine@julialetlow.com](mailto:katherine@julialetlow.com)
**NATIONAL RIGHT TO LIFE ENDORSES JULIA LETLOW FOR U.S. SENATE** _Nation’s largest grassroots pro-life organization backs Letlow in Louisiana Senate race_
**BATON ROUGE, LA** — Congresswoman Julia Letlow, the conservative candidate for U.S. Senate in Louisiana, announced that National Right to Life, the nation’s oldest and largest grassroots pro-life organization, has endorsed Congresswoman Julia Letlow for the United States Senate. The endorsement recognizes Letlow’s strong pro-life record in Congress and her commitment to defending the unborn and standing with Louisiana families.
_“National Right to Life is pleased to endorse Julia Letlow for the United States Senate,”_**said Carol Tobias, president of National Right to Life.**_“Throughout her service in the House of Representatives, Congresswoman Letlow has demonstrated an unwavering commitment to protecting innocent human life and supporting mothers and their children.”_
_“Julia Letlow understands that every human life has value and deserves protection,”_**Tobias continued.**_“Louisiana families can trust her to stand against the abortion industry’s radical agenda and to defend the most vulnerable members of our society.”_
_“The contrast in this election could not be more clear,”_**Tobias said.**_“Julia Letlow will defend Louisiana’s pro-life values in the United States Senate, while Jamie Davis would support efforts to impose abortion on demand through federal law.”_
_“Julia Letlow has earned the confidence and support of pro-life Louisianans,”_**Tobias added.**_“National Right to Life looks forward to working with Senator Julia Letlow to advance protections for unborn children and provide compassionate support for women and families.”_
_“As a mother, protecting the unborn is deeply personal to me, and I am incredibly honored to have the support of National Right to Life,”_ **said Letlow.**_“I have always been unapologetically pro-life, and my record in Congress reflects that commitment. In the U.S. Senate, I will continue fighting to defend the most vulnerable among us, protect the sanctity of life, and make sure mothers and families have the support they need.”_
Letlow has consistently stood for life throughout her time in Congress. Since 2021, she has earned a 100% pro-life voting record by backing protections for babies born alive after attempted abortions, opposing taxpayer-funded abortion, and voting to cut off federal funding for Planned Parenthood and other major abortion providers.
National Right to Life’s endorsement adds to the growing coalition supporting Letlow’s campaign for the United States Senate. They urged pro-life voters across Louisiana to support Letlow in the general election on November 3.

Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones is going after Greene County Sheriff Steven Smith after his office aided U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement in June during an operation that resulted in around 50 arrests.

Jones calls the traffic stops potential violations of "state law and the Constitution. Jones' office is requiring the Greene County Sheriff's Office to turn over all documents and policies regarding traffic stops and immigration enforcement.

clean_body: This is bigger than one state | | | | Derek, here's why Wisconsin's governor's race deserves your attention even if you've never set foot in the state. 1️⃣ Wisconsin is one of only five governorships Democrats are defending this year in a state Donald Trump carried in 2024. 2️⃣ Wisconsin has decided the last three presidential elections by less than a single point each time. 3️⃣ Whoever wins the governor's mansion here has real power over voting access, reproductive rights, and whether Trump's agenda hits a wall or a rubber stamp at the state line. Governor Tony Evers isn't running again, so this is the first open governor's race in Wisconsin since 2002, and we officially have our nominee. Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley is the exact candidate who can beat MAGA Tom Tiffany in November. He's spent his career building coalitions, getting things done, and winning the votes of Democrats, Independents, and Republicans. Tom Tiffany, on the other hand, is a Trump-endorsed Congressman with a five-year record of voting for abortion bans, Medicaid cuts, and education funding cuts. Peter -

I never expected to be running for office. I have never had any desire to be a politician. I am doing this because I am answering President Donald Trump's call to serve and want to stand up for South Carolina and fight for his agenda.

_**Like Lindsey, I am a hard worker with a servant's heart.**_ We grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. Our parents worked hard every day to make ends meet - there was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in.

What I've spent my life doing is serving South Carolina - including running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget. We turned it from a struggling organization into a national model helping people find work and live independently. We made sure all spending was reasonable, allowable, and necessary. _I fought against duplication of services, knowing it wasted taxpayers' dollars_.

clean_body: I am answering President Donald Trump's call to serve and want to stand up for South Carolina and fight for his agenda. | Peter - I never expected to be running for office. I have never had any desire to be a politician. I am doing this because I am answering President Donald Trump's call to serve and want to stand up for South Carolina and fight for his agenda. Like Lindsey, I am a hard worker with a servant's heart. We grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. Our parents worked hard every day to make ends meet - there was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in. What I've spent my life doing is serving South Carolina - including running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget. We turned it from a struggling organization into a national model helping people find work and live independently. We made sure all spending was reasonable, allowable, and necessary. I fought against duplication of services, knowing it wasted taxpayers' dollars. I'm a mother, a grandmother, and a wife, and now South Carolina's first female United States Senator, I know how to bargain shop, and I look for the buy-one-get-one-free sales at the grocery store. I just bought a new pair of shoes to walk around the U.S. Capitol off the clearance rack at the Shoe Warehouse. I cut my own grass with a push mower, and yes, I know how to use a weed eater. I support the Right to Life. I believe in showing ID to vote to save our country. I oppose DEI. I think AOC is C-R-A-Z-Y. I think Anthony Fauci should stop staring at the floor and answer the questions. I stand for the national anthem. I believe our veterans are heroes. I will always Back the Blue. And I know that President Trump and I will Make America Great Again. I am the first woman United States senator in South Carolina history. My Democratic opponent, Dr. Annie Andrews, must not be the second. She supports turning confused little boys into little girls and vice versa. I believe that makes her the worst pediatrician in the country. President Trump wants a fighter in the Senate. That's exactly why he's in my corner in this race. Thanks, Darline Graham P.S. Hey y’all,
I've been back on the ground in Memphis, knocking doors and talking to voters in their neighborhoods. And I want to tell you what I'm hearing.
[](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/0UyKvwyfb75uaBeEeDMT2g~~/AAUS1hA~/5EJxAy87fhQWTJ8fAN1DSK7g3-vpPyF5PrD6bknajVBxHwTBz-U0_1PQoYFtB3qnon3PeUnFroso8P3tRxUDtl1jvTVw0P8_YAiVOCNgxeIjL9vZCLX6FCSCVzjH_VJQnM7WXIJP479bhH7eYP1dT6m9RYNDRuWmMFj1vmBLO8n82IcI7jetgREc2mGFDON2vycWl2iwwmRT3gVypshZgdnZ_KChls7SQLd1GC0Wcmo5efQp3x_v-Nx7bjem7Ue7)

And a recent AARP poll shows a 3-point lead for Democrats in the generic ballot. Right now, far-right lawmakers in Phoenix are championing policies that hurt everyday families — defunding our public schools through a runaway voucher program costing taxpayers over $1 billion, attacking reproductive freedom, and blocking critical investments in healthcare and water security. Team, we don't have to accept this as our reality. In competitive districts across our state, dynamic leaders are stepping up to fight for us: In LD2 , Dr. Amelia Gallitano is running for Senate to reform the voucher system and protect access to quality healthcare. In LD4 , Aaron Lieberman is running to restore funding to public education, while Karen Gresham and Tammy Caputi fight for real economic accountability in the House. In LD13 , educator Rockee Armstrong and combat veteran Jacob Weinberg are running to invest in our schools, protect our local water supply, and lower costs. In LD17 , Rep. Kevin Volk and retired Air Force Col. Holly Lyon are leading the charge to keep housing affordable and protect our water future. In LD23 , Emilia Cortez is taking on an incumbent who won by just 592 votes in 2024. The margins in these districts are razor-thin. body:
Please do not click away

**$3, Please.**
That is the contribution I am asking you to rush - and I mean rush - to Stefany Shaheen's campaign for Congress in New Hampshire.
**Please do not click away -- because this is probably one of the more strategic contributions you can make at this point in the election.**
As you know, we have a chance to effectively end the Trump presidency in November – if the American people are given a fair chance to elect enough Democrats to take back Congress.
But that means winning the tough races. The races Republicans will target to hold power.
And one of those races is Stefany's. Hers is a district Trump only lost by one percent and New Hampshire is a state recent polling has shown Republicans making large gains.
So please - $3.
$3 - because we have to win this race if Democrats are going to take back the House of Representatives this November.
$3 - because we can replace a Republican governor and both chambers of the legislature that are controlled by Republicans.

In honor of Women's Equality Day, we're remembering what Dolly Parton did with her seat at the table. |
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138060938/642833547/-870569556?sourceid=1059912&refcode=WUEFET90_20260827_DollyRS_PLEXP&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyODg0OTc1MC02YmEyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTliZWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=t9evbi4YQ8mujNK5ToswewzufflFvPz1EEZVOvQynR8=) Peter, Tuesday we lost Dolly Parton. Yesterday was Women's Equality Day. It feels almost too fitting to be a coincidence. Dolly Parton came from the Smoky Mountains and built an extraordinary life on her own talent and her own terms, in an industry that rarely made room for women to do either. But what made her legacy so remarkable wasn't simply the power she built. It was what she did with it. She gave books to millions of children. She invested in her home state and created jobs for her neighbors. She put significant funding behind the COVID-19 vaccine. Again and again, Dolly used her seat at the table to make room for others. **[Dolly embodied what we believe about women in leadership: When women have a seat at the table, they can lift entire communities with them.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138060939/642833548/-870569556?sourceid=1059912&refcode=WUEFET90_20260827_DollyRS_PLEXP&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyODg0OTc1MC02YmEyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTliZWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=t9evbi4YQ8mujNK5ToswewzufflFvPz1EEZVOvQynR8=)** | [ELECT WOMEN](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138060940/642833549/1425818251?sourceid=1059912&refcode=WUEFET90_20260827_DollyRS_PLEXP&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyODg0OTc1MC02YmEyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTliZWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=t9evbi4YQ8mujNK5ToswewzufflFvPz1EEZVOvQynR8=)

And on Women's Equality Day, that feels particularly worth remembering. The 19th Amendment was a milestone, not a finish line. Women remain underrepresented at every level of government — and across much of the South, Democratic pro-choice women still face especially steep barriers to winning office.
That makes Dolly's story as a daughter of Appalachia especially powerful. She came from a region where the path to power for women has never been easy, reached extraordinary heights, and spent a lifetime using that power to empower others.
Across the South today, EMILYs List is working to make sure more women have the chance to do the same. That's why, this cycle, we’re proud to endorse dozens of women candidates across eight southern states.

clean_body: In honor of Women's Equality Day, we're remembering what Dolly Parton did with her seat at the table. | = Peter, Tuesday we lost Dolly Parton. Yesterday was Women's Equality Day. It feels almost too fitting to be a coincidence. Dolly Parton came from the Smoky Mountains and built an extraordinary life on her own talent and her own terms, in an industry that rarely made room for women to do either. But what made her legacy so remarkable wasn't simply the power she built. It was what she did with it. She gave books to millions of children. She invested in her home state and created jobs for her neighbors. She put significant funding behind the COVID-19 vaccine. Again and again, Dolly used her seat at the table to make room for others. = | = And on Women's Equality Day, that feels particularly worth remembering. The 19th Amendment was a milestone, not a finish line. Women remain underrepresented at every level of government — and across much of the South, Democratic pro-choice women still face especially steep barriers to winning office. That makes Dolly's story as a daughter of Appalachia especially powerful. She came from a region where the path to power for women has never been easy, reached extraordinary heights, and spent a lifetime using that power to empower others. Across the South today, EMILYs List is working to make sure more women have the chance to do the same. That's why, this cycle, we’re proud to endorse dozens of women candidates across eight southern states. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Today, and every day, let's carry Dolly’s spirit forward. It's a sad truth that Jewish Americans have experienced antisemitism throughout history - but over the last few years, we're seeing the worst surge of anti-Jewish violence and harassment in decades.
Like nearly every other Jewish American, I've experienced antisemitism firsthand. When I was just a few years old, I was playing in a hotel swimming pool with my mom while on vacation when a lifeguard on duty told her that we were "dirty" because we were Jewish - and that we had to leave the pool immediately because of it. My parents packed up our things and left that hotel. We never returned. My mom never forgot that interaction, retelling the story for years. It's a feeling no one should have to experience.
**Now, I fear more and more American Jewish families are coming face to face with violence every week: Our communities are being impacted by mass shootings, threatening graffiti, physical assaults, and firebombings.**
All of it is wrong, and addressing this kind of violent antisemitism is an issue I've been working on since before I came to Congress and throughout my time in the House and Senate. That is why:
* I founded the Senate's first ever Bipartisan Task Force for Combating Antisemitism, which now includes more than half the Senate as members.
* I just introduced the Jewish American Security Act - sweeping legislation to fight antisemitism on college campuses, at Jewish communal institutions, and online. The bill is supported by the American Jewish Committee, the ADL, and the Jewish Council for Public Affairs.
* I successfully pushed the Biden administration to create the first-ever National Strategy to Counter Antisemitism, which took a whole-of-government approach to tackling rising hate.
* I led the effort in Congress to increase the power of the State Department's Special Envoy to Monitor and Combat Antisemitism by raising the position to the rank of Ambassador.
* I introduced and successfully helped pass legislation reauthorizing the Never Again Education Act to educate communities about the Holocaust.
* I successfully pressured the Trump administration to avoid weakening Coast Guard standards for hate symbols like swastikas.

As only the third Jewish woman elected to the U.S. Senate in our nation's 250-year- history - and the first former synagogue president ever elected - I strive to be a leading voice in the Senate to combat antisemitism. This means living up to and practicing the value of tikkun olam - taking action to repair the world - through advocacy and legislation.
No one in this country should be discriminated against because of their faith or who they are - and it's the responsibility of those in Congress to take action to protect Jewish Americans - on college campuses, in their homes and places of worship, in the military, and everywhere.
**The work is personal and urgent: We can 't let our country regress toward one of human civilization's darkest chapters. [I'm grateful to supporters like you for giving to help power the fight for a country that is safe for all.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/385d7b14-3b44-4392-ab4a-fc5820dae19d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Thanks for your partnership in this fight,
Jacky

clean_body: We have a shared responsibility to repair the world - and that means taking action. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more We have a shared responsibility to repair the world - and that means taking action. | | | Aug 27 | | | | | | | | | | | | It's a sad truth that Jewish Americans have experienced antisemitism throughout history - but over the last few years, we're seeing the worst surge of anti-Jewish violence and harassment in decades. Like nearly every other Jewish American, I've experienced antisemitism firsthand. When I was just a few years old, I was playing in a hotel swimming pool with my mom while on vacation when a lifeguard on duty told her that we were "dirty" because we were Jewish - and that we had to leave the pool immediately because of it. My parents packed up our things and left that hotel. We never returned. My mom never forgot that interaction, retelling the story for years. It's a feeling no one should have to experience. Now, I fear more and more American Jewish families are coming face to face with violence every week: Our communities are being impacted by mass shootings, threatening graffiti, physical assaults, and firebombings. All of it is wrong, and addressing this kind of violent antisemitism is an issue I've been working on since before I came to Congress and throughout my time in the House and Senate. That is why: I founded the Senate's first ever Bipartisan Task Force for Combating Antisemitism, which now includes more than half the Senate as members. I just introduced the Jewish American Security Act - sweeping legislation to fight antisemitism on college campuses, at Jewish communal institutions, and online. The bill is supported by the American Jewish Committee, the ADL, and the Jewish Council for Public Affairs. I successfully pushed the Biden administration to create the first-ever National Strategy to Counter Antisemitism, which took a whole-of-government approach to tackling rising hate. I led the effort in Congress to increase the power of the State Department's Special Envoy to Monitor and Combat Antisemitism by raising the position to the rank of Ambassador. I introduced and successfully helped pass legislation reauthorizing the Never Again Education Act to educate communities about the Holocaust. I successfully pressured the Trump administration to avoid weakening Coast Guard standards for hate symbols like swastikas. As only the third Jewish woman elected to the U.S. Senate in our nation's 250-year- history - and the first former synagogue president ever elected - I strive to be a leading voice in the Senate to combat antisemitism. This means living up to and practicing the value of tikkun olam - taking action to repair the world - through advocacy and legislation. No one in this country should be discriminated against because of their faith or who they are - and it's the responsibility of those in Congress to take action to protect Jewish Americans - on college campuses, in their homes and places of worship, in the military, and everywhere. The work is personal and urgent: We can 't let our country regress toward one of human civilization's darkest chapters. Thanks for your partnership in this fight, Jacky * `A personal note from Sen. Jacky Rosen:` `My work in the Senate has always been defined by who I am and where I come from. Growing up as the granddaughter of immigrants and the daughter of a World War II veteran, my family instilled in me the values of hard work, determination, and persistence at a young age.` `Now, I'm proud to fight tirelessly in the Senate to deliver progress for hardworking families like mine in Nevada and across our country. But with Donald Trump in the White House and Republicans in control of both houses of Congress, I need your grassroots support to keep up the fights that matter most.` `Senate Democrats like me are the only thing standing in the way of Trump's extreme agenda that will hurt everyday Americans. **I’m a product of the American Dream.**

But it’s becoming increasingly harder to forge a better life. College tuition has tripled, healthcare is more expensive than ever, and the middle class is disappearing right before our eyes.

As a journalist for forty years, I’ve always sought to hold power accountable. From covering stories about addiction to offshoring jobs to civil rights, I’ve never been afraid to ruffle feathers and tell the unvarnished truth.

**It’s that passion for listening and honesty that I will bring with me to Congress to fight for the people of VA-06. And it’s never been more needed.**
